Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Dissolve 2g low-melting temperature agarose in 100mL sterilized distilled water
2. Heat mixture in microwave with interval shaking to dissolve agarose completely
3. Add 520μL melted agarose to 256-well-format mold
4. Allow agarose in mold to solidify
5. Transfer agarose microplate to single well of 12-well plate
6. Add 1.5mL DPBS with calcium and magnesium to each well
7. Pipette DPBS up and down to remove bubbles
8. Aspirate medium from undifferentiated human pluripotent stem cell (HPSC) culture
9. Add 5 mL room-temperature calcium/magnesium-free DPBS to rinse cells
10. Remove DPBS buffer after rinsing
11. Add 5 mL cell dissociation reagent to cells
12. Incubate at 37°C for 6-8 minutes
13. Observe cell detachment under microscope
14. Remove cell dissociation reagent
15. Add 5 mL fresh MT serve one medium to stop reaction
16. Remove cell dissociation reagent to stop reaction
17. Add 5 mL of fresh MT serve one medium supplemented with 10 μM rock inhibitor Y27632
18. Pipette mixture up and down several times to dissociate cells
19. Count viable cells using hemocytometer and trypan blue staining
20. Transfer desired number of cells to sterile 15 mL or 50 mL centrifuge tube
21. Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 minutes to pellet cells
22. Discard supernatant
23. Resuspend cell pellet in MT serve one medium with 10 μM rock inhibitor at 2.1 million cells/mL concentration
24. Add 190 microliters of prepared cell suspension per agarose microwell
25. Incubate agarose microplates at 37°C in 5% CO₂ for 2 hours
26. Add 1 mL of fresh warm T-serve one medium with rock inhibitor to each well
27. Return plates to incubator for 24-hour incubation
28. Examine hepatosphere formation
29. Dissolve 2 grams of poly-HEMA in 100 milliliters of 95% ethanol
30. Stir solution overnight on 55°C hot plate
31. Add 250 microliters of solution to each well of 24-well plate
32. Dry plate overnight in 60°C oven
33. Remove MT serve one medium from previously seeded cells
34. Add 1 ml of fresh endoderm differentiation medium to cells
35. Refresh endoderm differentiation medium every 24 hours for 3 days
36. Switch medium to hepatoblast differentiation medium
37. Replace hepatoblast differentiation medium every 2 days for 5 days (including final change on last day)
38. Wash hepatospheres with hepatocyte maturation medium
39. Add 1 mL hepatocyte maturation medium supplemented with 10 ng/mL HGF and 20 ng/mL OSM
40. Pipette solution up and down several times to lift hepatospheres from agarose microplate
41. Transfer hepatospheres to poly-HEMA coated well
42. Wash agarose microplate with 1 mL supplemented hepatocyte maturation medium
43. Transfer wash medium to poly-HEMA coated well
44. Aspirate excess medium using P-100 pipette until approximately 1 milliliter remains in well, avoiding hepatosphere removal
45. Refresh medium every 48 hours for 12 days
46. Remove maturation medium (for embryonic stem cells at day 20)
47. Wash cells with maintenance medium
48. Add 1 milliliter of supplemented maintenance medium
49. Refresh medium every 48 hours after medium switch

22. Add six milliliters of PBS to dish

35. Remove tube from rotator
36. Place tube on magnetic rack
37. Remove lysis buffer
38. Combine 4 mg HEK293 protein extract with oligo(dT)25-coupled magnetic beads
39. Mix samples vigorously
40. Incubate mixture for 10 minutes at 25°C
41. Place tubes on magnetic stand for 10 seconds
42. Remove supernatant
43. Keep supernatant on ice for subsequent recovery rounds
44. Add 500 microliters of wash buffer A to beads
45. Vortex mixture for five seconds
46. Collect beads using magnet
47. Wash beads twice with 500 microliters of wash buffer B
48. Add 30 microliters of 10-millimolar Tris-HCl to beads
49. Incubate tube at 80 degrees Celsius for two minutes with continuous shaking at 1,000 RPM
50. Transfer tube to magnetic stand and collect eluate within 10 seconds to prevent RNA rebinding
51. Add 30 microliters of streptavidin-coupled magnetic beads to 1 mL binding and wash buffer containing 0.1 mg/mL E. coli tRNA
52. Equilibrate bead mixture on rotator for 1 hour at room temperature
53. Wash beads three times with 750 microliters binding and wash buffer
54. Vortex tube containing washed beads
55. Remove binding and wash buffer from tube
56. Resuspend beads in 30 microliters buffer
57. Store resuspended beads on ice until use
58. Dilute approximately 35 micrograms of total protein from poly(A) isolation in 100 microliters of binding and wash buffer
59. Add 200 picomoles of appropriate antisense oligonucleotide
60. Incubate mixture at 70 degrees Celsius for 5 minutes to facilitate annealing
61. Remove heat block from device and place at room temperature for 10 minutes to cool slowly
62. Add 30 microliters of equilibrated streptavidin-coupled magnetic beads to sample
63. Incubate mixture for 30 minutes at 25 degrees Celsius with constant shaking at 950 rpm
64. Place tube on magnetic stand and remove supernatant
65. Wash beads three times with 750 microliters of pre-warmed binding and wash buffer at 55 degrees Celsius
66. Add 20 microliters of 10-millimolar Tris-HCl
67. Place sample at 90 degrees Celsius with constant shaking at 950 rpm for 10 minutes to elute RNA
68. Place tube in magnetic stand
69. Immediately collect eluate

38. Centrifuge at 470 x gravity for 5 minutes at room temperature
39. Remove supernatant after centrifugation

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Pick 30 to 40 young adult worms into watch glass dish containing 500 microliters of 1x M9 and levamisole
2. Remove and discard most media to eliminate transferred bacteria
3. Add 500 microliters fresh 1x M9 and levamisole
4. Rinse worms by gently drawing and dispensing media with pipette
5. Remove and discard most media after rinsing
6. Repeat wash cycle (steps 3-5) two to three times
7. Leave worms in approximately 100 microliters media for ≤8 minutes
8. Transfer worms to 25-millimeter-by-75-millimeter microscope slide coated with 0.001% poly-L-lysine using glass or polyethylene pipette
9. Remove excess media until approximately 15 microliters remains on slide
10. Position two 26 1/2-gauge needles crossed in scissor formation under dissecting microscope
11. Cut worms behind pharynx using crossed needles to release germlines
12. Complete dissection of all worms within five minutes
13. Place 22-millimeter-by-40-millimeter coverslip perpendicularly over slide with ends hanging off
14. Freeze slides on pre-chilled aluminum block maintained on dry ice for at least 20 minutes
15. Place chilled pencil on top of coverslip to prevent displacement from ice expansion
16. Flick off coverslips with a pencil
17. Dip slide into jar of fresh ice-cold methanol for 1 minute
18. Gently wipe edges of slide surrounding sample
19. Apply 150 microliters of formaldehyde fixative at room temperature for 5 minutes
20. Touch slide to paper towel at 90-degree angle to drain fixative
21. Block slides twice for 15 minutes at room temperature
22. Absorb solution into paper towel
23. Block slides twice for 15 minutes at room temperature in Coplin jar with 50 ml PBT/BSA
24. Block slides with PBT/BSA solution containing 10% normal goat serum
25. Gently wipe edges surrounding slide
26. Apply 100 microliters of solution to each slide
27. Gently agitate slide to spread solution
28. Incubate for one hour at room temperature in humid chamber
29. Place slide on paper towel to let solution run off
30. Gently wipe slide edges
31. Apply one drop of blocking reagent to 14mm×14mm space
32. Incubate slides for one hour at 37°C in humid chamber
33. Gently wipe slide edges
34. Dilute primary antibodies using antibody diluent
35. Apply 40 microliters of diluted primary antibody solution per 14-by-14-millimeter space on slides
36. Place slides in humid chamber
37. Incubate slides overnight at 4°C
38. Wash slides twice for 5 minutes each with 50 ml of 1x wash buffer A at room temperature in Coplin jar
39. Set Coplin jar on orbital shaker at 60 rpm
40. Place slides on paper towel to drain wash buffer
41. Gently wipe slide edges
42. Prepare 40-microliter solution containing plus and minus probes
43. Add probe solution to each 14x14 mm space
44. Incubate slides in humid chamber for 1 hour at 37°C
45. Wash slides twice for 5 minutes each with 50 mL of 1x wash buffer A at room temperature in Coplin jar
46. Set Coplin jar on orbital shaker at 60 rpm
47. Dilute ligation buffer 1:5 with ultrapure water
48. Dilute ligase 1:40 using diluted buffer to prepare ligation solution
49. Place slide on paper towel to drain wash buffer
50. Gently wipe slide edges
51. Add 40 μL ligation solution to each 14x14 mm space
52. Incubate slides in humid chamber for 30 minutes at 37°C
53. Add 40 microliters of freshly prepared light-protected amplification solution to each 14-by-14-millimeter space
54. Incubate slides in humid dark chamber at 37°C for 1 hour 40 minutes
55. Wash slides twice for 10 minutes each with 50 milliliters of 1x wash buffer B
56. Wash slides once for 1 minute with 50 milliliters of 0.01x wash buffer B
57. Add 10 microliters of mounting medium to each sample
58. Gently lay coverslip on sample allowing mounting medium to spread
59. Paint nail polish around coverslip edge to seal while avoiding movement
60. Let nail polish harden for at least 20 minutes at room temperature protected from light
61. Ensure sufficient water is present in chamber
62. Ensure slides are level inside chamber
63. Image extruded gonads on confocal microscope
64. Quantify images using Fiji/ImageJ workflow

2. Remove hyoid bone and surrounding soft tissues by finding eminence of greater horn, following horn with blade, and passing through contralateral side
3. Cut trachea at distal side approximately 15 centimeters from larynx using dissecting knife
4. Reserve removed mediastinal organs for next procedural step
5. Take previously discarded mediastinal organs
6. Search for thymus in mediastinal organs
7. Detach thymus from surrounding tissue using dissecting forceps
8. Cut thymus into butterfly shape using dissecting knife to create 1.5 cm thick slice
9. Shape thymus slice with Metzenbaum scissors into butterfly form (two 3x2 cm lobes connected by isthmus)
10. Suture thyroid to tracheal wall
11. Place simulated thyroid between first and third tracheal rings
12. Take needle holder
13. Take surgical forceps
14. Grab two zero silk suture
15. Suture thyroid with two lateral horizontal mattress stitches in each lobe to lateral portion of trachea
16. Pass needle only in superficial part of trachea
17. Remove esophagus from larynx connection using scalpel or surgical scissors
18. Cut and open esophagus longitudinally with surgical scissors
19. Hold muscle and mucosa with tooth forceps during cutting
20. Suture esophagus to trachea
21. Place muscle layer on trachea and larynx with mucous membrane face up
22. Suture opened esophagus with six simple stitches
23. Place proximal suture on thyroid cartilage summit
24. Place distal suture on frontal partition of last tracheal ring
25. Mark a line on esophagus mucosa with white India ink to simulate linea alba using insulin syringe
26. Withdraw India ink into insulin syringe
27. Track line on simulated fascia by scratching mucosa with needle while dispensing ink drops
28. Remove excess ink gently using small swab
29. Cut foam square to dimensions 3 cm × 10 cm × 15 cm
30. Shape central furrow measuring 2.5 cm wide × 10 cm long
31. Fold foam square in half to create longitudinal hump
32. Cut 1 cm off entire length of hump using scissors
33. Unfold foam and trim furrow edges smoothly
34. Take wooden tablet matching foam dimensions
35. Place foam square on wooden tablet
36. Insert model into foam furrow
37. Staple tracheal end with wood stapler
38. Staple thyroid cartilage lateral muscles
39. Staple epiglottis
40. Take pig skin collected from butcher shop
41. Cut skin into 25x20 cm square shape to cover model
42. Cover model with skin using dissecting knife
43. Staple skin to wooden tablet with 10-15 clips using stapler

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Sort male and female mosquito pupae by size differences
2. Transfer 100 male pupae into pre-labeled cage
3. Transfer female pupae in batches of 40-50 per cage
4. Check cages for presence of male mosquitoes after adult emergence
5. Dissolve 200 milligrams of Rhodamine B powder in 100 milliliters of 10% sucrose solution
6. Mix solution thoroughly to ensure complete dissolution of powder
7. Prepare 20 sugar feeder bottles with wicks
8. Add 10 milliliters of 10% sucrose solution to 10 feeder bottles
9. Add 10 milliliters of 0.2% Rhodamine B sucrose solution to the remaining 10 feeder bottles
10. Place five feeder bottles into each prepared male cage
11. Allow male mosquitoes to feed from bottles for three days
12. Turn on mercury burner lamp
13. Turn on stereo microscope
14. Allow mercury burner lamp to stabilize for 10 minutes
15. Set fluorescence filters to red fluorescence protein one (RFP1)
16. Aspirate small number of mosquitoes into oral aspirator glass tube
17. Observe male mosquito bodies through glass tube under fluorescent stereo microscope to verify Rhodamine B marking
18. Transfer set A male mosquitoes: Place 10 sucrose-fed males per cup into six net-secured paper cups
19. Transfer set A male mosquitoes: Place 10 Rhodamine B sucrose-fed males per cup into six net-secured paper cups
20. Repeat transfer and grouping procedure for set B male mosquitoes
21. Set up 12 mating cages
22. Add mosquitoes to cages: For 6 cages - 10 Rhodamine B marked set A males, 10 unmarked set B males, 10 virgin wild-type females. For other 6 cages - 10 unmarked set A males, 10 Rhodamine B marked set B males, 10 virgin wild-type females
23. Label cages to distinguish mating combinations
24. Place respective male cups in mating cages according to labels
25. Remove netting and gently tap cup to release males
26. Allow male mosquitoes to acclimate in mating cage for at least 1 hour
27. Transfer virgin wild-type female mosquitoes into 12 paper cups using an oral aspirator
28. Transfer one cup of females into every mating cage and remove netting
29. Gently jostle cup to encourage remaining female mosquitoes out
30. Remove paper cup and netting from cage to prevent mosquito escapes
31. Allow mating to take place for three hours
32. Terminate mating experiment by removing all mosquitoes from each cage with mechanical aspirator
33. Cold-anesthetize mosquitoes on ice for at least five minutes
34. Gently pick up female mosquitoes and house them in separate netting-secured paper cup
35. Label paper cup by transferring respective label from mating cage
36. Cold-anesthetize female mosquitoes on ice for at least five minutes prior to dissection
37. Dissect female mosquito under stereo microscope
38. Examine spermathecae under microscope
39. Determine presence of Rhodamine B marked seminal fluid in spermathecae using fluorescent stereo microscope with RFP1 filter

3. Intubate with 6.5 millimeter tube
4. Use syringe to inflate tube cuff with 3-5 milliliters of air
5. Ensure tracheal tube is in proper position
6. Apply ointment to animal's eyes
7. Protect eyes with cover patch
8. Disinfect neck and abdominal wall with 1% iodine-based scrub solution
9. Make vertical midline anterior neck incision to sternum using number 23 blade
10. Dissect strap muscles
11. Retract muscles laterally using Kelly tissue scissors and Lahey retractor to expose trachea from first ring to thoracic inlet
12. Expose common carotid artery and internal jugular vein for anastomosis
13. Create 1 cm window in second or third tracheal cartilage using number 11 blade

15. Design flap on upper abdomen using surgical marking pen
16. Create 4x3 cm elliptical skin incision through anterior sheath using #23 scalpel
17. Position incision on medial side of flap
18. Hold fascia with Allis clamp
19. Elevate flap from rectus abdominis muscle sheath
20. Locate perforators going to skin flap
21. Perform blunt dissection of exposed muscle tissue
22. Follow perforators to superior epigastric vessels
23. Make lateral skin incision in flap using number 23 scalpel
24. Clamp superior epigastric vessels and venae comitantes with haemostat
25. Cut above haemostat using Kelly tissue scissors
26. Ligate vessel below haemostat with three-oh suture to allow haemostat removal
27. Clamp carotid artery with two haemostats placed 1-2 cm apart
28. Cut between haemostats using microscissors
29. Tie superior part of vessel with double suture to prevent leakage
30. Place first two stay sutures 120 degrees apart around vessel circumference using 10-0 simple full thickness interrupted suture
31. Place 2-3 stitches between stay sutures
32. Release vascular clamp
33. Check anastomosis for leakage
34. Create anastomosis between internal jugular vein and venae comitantes
35. Prick skin flap with 18-gauge needle syringe to test viability
36. Observe for blood droplet appearance at puncture site
37. Close tracheal window using 3-0 suture with muscle fascia of superior epigastric artery perforator flap
38. Exteriorize skin panel of flap
39. Suture flap skin panel to cervical midline skin incision

41. Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 minutes
42. Discard supernatant
43. Add 50 μL complete culture medium to cell pellet
44. Mix well to resuspend cells
45. Add 140 μL matrix extract to cell suspension
46. Gently mix to avoid air bubbles
47. Pipette 50 μL aliquots to create domes in prewarmed 6-well plate

49. Flip 6-well plate upside down

1. Homogenize 100 grams of fresh radish using kitchen blender for 10 minutes
2. Transfer resulting slurry to 50 milliliter centrifuge tube
3. Centrifuge at 14,000 × g at 4°C for 20 minutes to remove insoluble material
4. Transfer supernatant to new 50 milliliter centrifuge tube
5. Add equal volume of 2M trichloroacetic acid solution
6. Centrifuge at 14,000 × g at 4°C for 30 minutes
7. Remove supernatant
8. Wash pellet with 20mL deionized water
9. Centrifuge at 14,000 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes
10. Resuspend pellet in 1mL deionized water
11. Transfer protein solution to fresh 1.5mL centrifuge tube
12. Mix 50 microliters of protein solution with 0.2 milliunits of recombinant PNGase H+ in ten millimolar acetic acid
13. Incubate mixture at 37 degrees Celsius for 12 hours
14. Centrifuge mixture at 14,000 × g for five minutes to remove residual protein and enzyme
15. Transfer supernatant to fresh 1.5 milliliter centrifuge tube
16. Wash solid phase extraction column with 3 mL water
17. Activate column with 3 mL of 80% acetonitrile containing trifluoroacetic acid
18. Equilibrate column with 3 mL deionized water
19. Transfer sample onto column
20. Discard flow-through
21. Wash column with 1.5 mL deionized water
22. Add 1.5 milliliters of aqueous 20% acetonitrile solution containing 0.1% TFA to elute N-glycans into a two milliliter tube
23. Remove solvent by centrifugal evaporation at room temperature
24. Evaporate sample until completely dry
25. Add 5 microliters of prepared 2-AB solution to dried samples
26. Vortex samples until completely dissolved
27. Incubate samples at 65 degrees Celsius for 2 hours
28. Cool samples to room temperature for 5 minutes
29. Add 5 microliters of deionized water and 40 microliters of acetonitrile to cooled samples
30. Centrifuge samples at 14,000 × g for 3 minutes
31. Transfer 48 microliters of supernatant to 300 microliter HPLC vial
32. Store samples at -20 degrees Celsius
33. Connect UPLC glycan column to online fluorescence detector
34. Set fluorescence detector excitation wavelength to 330 nm and emission wavelength to 420 nm
35. Set column temperature to 60 degrees Celsius
36. Inject 45 microliters of sample into UPLC system
37. Elute N-glycans by UPLC using 15-40 minute retention window
38. Collect each UPLC peak fraction into 2-milliliter centrifuge tubes
39. Dry samples using centrifugal evaporation
40. Inject 1 picomole of 2-AB labeled dextran standard for calibration, elution time assignment, and glucose unit standardization
41. Dissolve dried samples in 5 microliters of LCMS grade water
42. Mix 1 microliter of dissolved sample with 1 microliter of ATT solution
43. Pipet mixture into MALDI-TOF sample carrier
44. Load sample carrier into MALDI-TOF mass spectrometer for analysis

12. Sort plastic pellets by color using tweezers

15. Switch on the pressurized fluid extractor
16. Download the extraction method
17. Warm up instrument to 60 degrees centigrade
18. Place bottom filter and frit in extraction cell
19. Close extraction cell
20. Fill approximately half the cell with ultra-clean quartz sand using funnel
21. Add 10 weighed pellets to extraction cell
22. Add quartz sand up to one centimeter to top of cell
23. Insert top filter into cell
24. Place cell in instrument
25. Place collecting vessels in instrument
26. Start extraction method
27. Empty extraction cell into cleaned glass Petri dish
28. Retrieve 10 pellets from sand
29. Store pellets for plastic identification analysis
30. Transfer extract from collecting vessel to glass tube
31. Concentrate extract in rotating concentrator at 35°C for 20 minutes
32. Place waste tube in rack and Florisil cartridge on manifold in closed-valve position
33. Turn on vacuum source

35. Open valve to allow solvent to pass through entire sorbent bed
36. Close valve

38. Open valve to let sorbent pass through
39. Close valve before sorbent dries off

Question: Given the complete step list of the experiment, please predict the next step that will take place after experimental steps shown in this video.
Complete step list: Sterilize cover slips with 70% ethanol for 2 minutes
2. Air dry sterilized cover slips
3. Place each cover slip into 10 cm culture plate
4. Add 300 microliters warm gelatin solution to center of cover slip (avoiding edges)
5. Aspirate gelatin solution after 5 minutes incubation
6. Harvest confluent human umbilical vein endothelial cells using 0.25% trypsin-EDTA
7. Count cells and pellet by centrifugation
8. Aspirate supernatant media
9. Resuspend cell pellets in basic nuclear effector solution
10. Add 0.2-2 micrograms of GFP beta actin vector plasmid
11. Transfer 100 microliters of cell suspension to nuclear effector cuvette
12. Tap covered cuvette to eliminate bubbles between bottom and sample
13. Place cuvette into nuclear effector device
14. Run program A034 on device
15. Add 500 microliters of warmed EGM2-MV media to cuvette using transfer pipette
16. Transfer mixture back to microcentrifuge tube
17. Incubate mixture for 15 minutes
18. Gently mix transfected VE suspension once
19. Seed 300 microliters of suspension onto gelatin-coated cover slip without touching edges
20. Incubate for one to four hours
21. Inspect transfected cells to confirm attachment to cover slip
22. Add 10 milliliters of E GM two MV media to plate
23. Continue incubation for GFP actin expression
24. Add albumin physiological salt solution (PSS) to gravity flow system
25. Connect gravity flow system to inline heater
26. Adjust flow regulator to achieve 40 milliliters per hour flow rate
27. Close stop cock using cotton tipped applicator to stop flow
28. Apply vacuum grease to outer edge of underside of diamond bath
29. Remove transfected culture from incubator
30. Gently lift cover slip using forceps
31. Soak up excess EGM-2MV media from bottom slide using Kim wipe
32. Position cover slip with cells facing upward
33. Place diamond bath over cover slip to form chamber
34. Place chamber into stage heater
35. Tighten clamps over chamber
36. Pipette approximately 1 milliliter of EGM-2MV media from plate into chamber
37. Attach vacuum hose to holder on left side of chamber
38. Connect A-PSS line from inline heater to channel on right side of chamber
39. Turn on vacuum
40. Open A-PSS line to initiate bath perfusion over transfected cells
41. Switch on inline heater at 37 degrees Celsius
42. Place thermistor probe for heated stage into bath at edge
43. Switch on stage heater at 37 degrees Celsius
44. Wipe underside of cover slip using Kim wipe soaked with 70% ethanol
45. Wipe underside of cover slip using dry Kim wipe
46. Equilibrate transfected HU cells for 30 minutes
47. Lock microscope course adjustment
48. Focus microscope on selected culture cells
49. Set camera exposure time between 0.5-2 seconds based on GFP-actin signal intensity
50. Set interval and duration times for time-lapse experiment
51. Capture single test image with room lights off to evaluate settings
52. Initiate time-lapse image acquisition series
53. Draw single-pixel line perpendicular to cell edge
54. Extract region from each time-lapse image to generate kymograph montage

43. Begin automatic sorting of sample

13. Thaw plastic tube containing aliquot of frozen suspension of small lipid vesicles at room temperature
14. Vortex tube four times for 1-2 seconds using vortex mixer at maximum speed
15. Place 5 microliters of small lipid vesicle suspension onto surface of uncleaned glass coverslip to form small round droplet
16. Place glass coverslip in vacuum desiccator for 20 minutes
17. Store dried lipid film at room temperature for 4 minutes
18. Pipette 50 microliters of 10 millimolar HEPES buffer onto dry lipid film
19. Wait 5 minutes for GUV-MLV complex formation
20. Center glass coverslip on microscope stage
21. Pipette 300 microliters of HEPES buffer onto coverslip
22. Position droplet center above microscope objective
23. Transfer 50 microliters of GUV-MLV solution into HEPES solution

25. Round edges of borosilicate glass capillaries by placing capillary ends into candle flame
26. Pull at least three glass capillaries using automatic laser puller to achieve tip opening of approximately 0.3 microns diameter
27. Filter 5 mM calcium chloride solution in HEPES buffer using 0.2-0.5 micron syringe filter
28. Back-fill each micropipette with 8 microliters of filtered calcium chloride solution using Microloader
29. Connect micropipette holder to micromanipulator
30. Mount micropipette into micropipette holder tightly
31. Connect injection pump to system
32. Connect capillary holder using supply tube
33. Start injection pump
34. Adjust injection pump settings to 20 hectopascal injection pressure
35. Set compensation pressure to 5 hectopascal
36. Set microscope to bright-field mode
37. Configure microscope for differential interference contrast
38. Position micropipette above droplet containing GUV-MLV complexes using coarse micromanipulator
39. Locate the tip of the micropipette above the objective
40. Bring the micropipette down to the droplet using the coarse micromanipulator
41. Set the microscope to fluorescence mode
42. Position the micropipette tip at a distance of three microns from the membrane surface
43. Inject calcium chloride solution from the micropipette to allow MTPs to form
44. Translate micropipette tip around GUV surface using fine micromanipulator
45. Maintain constant distance between GUV surface and micropipette tip
46. Continue calcium ion injection during manipulation
47. Turn off injection pump to stop microinjection

17. Add two drops chloroform to supernatant

32. Incubate plate at 30°C until colonies appear

34. Incubate plates at 30°C until single colonies appear

36. Add 1 picogram of pCP20 plasmid DNA to cell suspension
37. Gently mix DNA-cell suspension
38. Transfer mixture to pre-cooled 1 mm electroporation cuvette
39. Set electroporator to 1.8 kilovolts
40. Perform electroporation

43. Plate 100 microliters of cells on LB plus ampicillin plates

1. Harvest spinal cord via laminectomy
2. Cut spinal cord transversely into 1 cm segments
3. Dissect paraventricular region from each spinal cord segment
4. Mince tissue into 1 mm pieces
5. Enzymatically dissociate minced tissue
6. Separate intact cells by centrifugation through discontinuous density gradient
7. Plate cell suspension
8. Sterilize rat's skin and remove dorsal surface using large dissection scissors to expose vertebral column
9. Hold dissection scissors perpendicular to dorsal surface and transversely cut vertebral column above hind limbs
10. Use small scissors to longitudinally cut dorsal muscle over vertebral column in rostral direction to expose spinous processes
11. Insert small blunt bone cutting instrument extraorally into lateral aspect of spinal canal between spinal cord and vertebral column starting at exposed caudal end
12. Place blade shallow and parallel to spinal cord
13. Make small cuts into lamina
14. Peel away lamina to expose spinal cord
15. Continue removing lamina in rostral direction to expose thoracic and cervical spinal cord
16. Using blunt tissue forceps, gently lift spinal cord from vertebral column
17. Sever spinal roots with micro scissors to release cord
18. Place excised spinal cord in Petri dish containing ice-cold sterile rat dissection buffer
19. Rinse tissue with ice cold dissecting buffer
20. Cut spinal cord transversely into 1cm segments using scissors
21. Hold tissue segment with fine forceps
22. Use micro scissors to carefully remove white matter and most gray matter
23. Isolate periventricular region of spinal cord
24. Transfer dissected periventricular tissue to 10cm sterile Petri dish containing ice cold rat dissection buffer
25. Mince dissected periventricular tissue into 1 cubic millimeter pieces using micro scissors
26. Add 5 milliliters of Earl's balanced salt solution to vial of papain from dissociation kit
27. Incubate vial at 37 degrees Celsius for 10 minutes until papain dissolves and solution appears clear
28. Add 500 microliters of Earl's balanced salt solution to vial of DNAs
29. Gently mix DNAs solution
30. Add 250 microliters of DNA solution to vial containing papain
31. Gently mix papain-DNA solution
32. Add approximately 0.2 grams minced tissue to vial
33. Place vial on rocker platform at 37 degrees Celsius for 45 minutes to one hour
34. Triturate mixture with 10 milliliter pipette to dissociate tissue pieces
35. Yield cloudy cell suspension
36. Transfer cell suspension into sterile 15 milliliter conical tube
37. Centrifuge at 300 G for 5 minutes at room temperature
38. Prepare OVO moid solution by mixing 2.7 milliliters of Earl's balanced salt solution with 300 microliters of reconstituted albumin OVO MOID inhibitor solution in 15 milliliter conical tube
39. Add 150 microliters of DNA solution to OVO moid solution
40. Mix solution by inverting tube
41. Discard supernatant from pelleted cells
42. Immediately resuspend cell pellet in diluted DNA albumin inhibitor mixture
43. Add 5 ml of albumin inhibitor solution to a 15 ml tube
44. Gently layer cell suspension on top of albumin inhibitor solution using a 5 ml pipette
45. Centrifuge sample at 70 g for 6 minutes at room temperature
46. Discard supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 1 ml of prewarmed rat EFH medium
47. Count live cell density using a hemocytometer
48. Plate cells into T25 culture flask at density of 10 cells/μl in EFH medium
49. Incubate flasks at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for one week without disturbance

46. Place tubes on magnetic rack for one minute

49. Resuspend beads in 200 microliters of proteinase K digestion buffer and 3.5 microliters of proteinase K
50. Incubate suspension for three hours at 50 degrees Celsius with shaking at 800 revolutions per minute
51. Extract RNA using 800 microliters of RNA extraction reagent via acid guanidinium thiocyanate phenol-chloroform protocol

prompt:
Question: Given the complete step list of the experiment, please predict the next step that will take place after experimental steps shown in this video.
Complete step list: Seed adipose-derived stromal cells (ASC) at approximately 80% confluency in conventional tissue culture plates
2. Seed ASC at approximately 80% confluency in PNIPAAm coated tissue culture plates of corresponding size
3. Maintain ASC in complete culture medium at 37°C and 5% CO₂
4. Change culture medium every two days
5. Wrap rim of plunger disk with lab tape at least two times to prevent leakage
6. Spray down 15 ml conical tube rack containing empty uncapped tubes with 70% ethanol in biosafety cabinet
7. Spray each tape-wrapped plunger with 70% ethanol and place into empty conical tube
8. Spray approximately 6.3 gram metal washers and place on rack with hooked forceps
9. Close cabinet sash and turn on UV light for overnight drying/sterilization
10. Add 0.75 grams of gelatin powder to 10 milliliters of HBSS
11. Balance solution pH with 100 microliters of sodium hydroxide
12. Place gelatin solution in 75-degree Celsius water bath
13. Shake tube vigorously every five minutes until powder dissolves
14. Strain homogeneous gelatin solution through syringe filter
15. Apply filtered gelatin solution to plungers
16. Allow gelatin to solidify in plunger mold
17. Unwrap tape from solidified gelatin mold
18. Remove gelatin from outer edge of plunger using hooked forceps
19. Ensure remaining central gelatin is completely level
20. Gently apply gelatin-removed plungers to PNIPAAm coated ASC plates
21. Use metal washers to weigh down plungers
22. Transfer plates to ice-water bath
23. Clean bottom of PNIPAAm coated plates to remove non-sterile water
24. Add cold cell culture medium to one 1.5 milliliter microcentrifuge tube per culture to be seeded
25. Wash large segments of adipose tissue three times in sterile PBS
26. Remove as much PBS as possible between washes
27. Coarsely mince tissue using forceps and sterile razor
28. Remove vasculature and fascia during mincing
29. Continue mincing until solution achieves thick liquid consistency with minimal visible tissue segments
30. Transfer minced tissue to prepared 1.5 ml tubes using modified P1000 micro-pipette tip
31. Briefly mix minced tissue with medium within tubes
32. Replace medium in each ASC culture with one volume of white adipose tissue solution
33. Transfer gelatin plungers to white adipose tissue mixture on base ASC plates
34. Examine monolayers in PNIPAAm coated plates under microscope to confirm cellular detachment
35. Move plates to 37-40°C heat block surface in biosafety cabinet
36. Add 2-3 milliliters of warmed culture medium to incubate cells and facilitate gelatin melting
37. Gently remove plungers from plate surface
38. Cover cultures with appropriate plate lids
39. Place plates in cell culture incubator
40. Aspirate and replace cell culture medium with phenol red-free M199 medium supplemented with insulin, dexamethasone, and antibiotics

1. Add 1 mg of fluorescently labeled compound to 100 microliters of deionized water
2. Dissolve 65 mg of PLGA in 750 microliters of dichloromethane in scintillation vial
3. Ultrasonicate mixture for 10-30 seconds at 160 watts to dissolve PLGA
4. Add entire first water phase to oil phase dropwise
5. Emulsify solution using handheld homogenizer at 20,000 rpm for 30 seconds
6. Add entire first water-oil phase dropwise into 15 ml of 1% PVA solution
7. Emulsify mixture as previously demonstrated
8. Transfer entire emulsion volume into 200 milliliter round-bottom flask
9. Remove solvent using rotary evaporator at 635 mmHg vacuum for 1 hour
10. Aliquot 1 milliliter of aqueous phase into each of 14 microcentrifuge tubes
11. Pellet microspheres by centrifugation
12. Remove 900 microliters of aqueous solution from each tube using micropipette without disturbing pellets
13. Wash microspheres with 1 milliliter de-ionized water
14. Remove 900 microliters of supernatant carefully
15. Seed 40 visually size-matched islets into one well of a 96-well tissue culture plate
16. Add 200 microliters of islet culture medium to the seeded well
17. Resuspend microspheres in pre-assay medium to achieve 10 nanograms per microliter compound concentration
18. Sonicate microspheres in ice water bath for 10 minutes at 160 watts with 10-second pulses at 4°C
19. Remove 100 microliters of islet culture medium from each well without dislodging islets
20. Add 100 microliters of microsphere-containing assay medium to each well
21. Carefully discard assay medium from all wells without disturbing islets
22. Gently wash islets with 200 microliters of PBS (two times)
23. Immerse islets in 100 microliters of trypsin EDTA solution
24. Incubate islets in trypsin EDTA for 3 minutes at room temperature
25. Perform gentle pipetting after 2 minutes of incubation
26. Transfer entire well volume into individual microcentrifuge tubes
27. Add 400 microliters of islet culture medium to each tube to stop dissociation
28. Centrifuge tubes to collect microsphere-treated islets
29. Remove supernatants gently using micropipette
30. Resuspend pellets in 200 microliters of fresh islet culture medium
31. Spin dissociated islets onto charged microscope slides using cytocentrifuge
32. Draw boundary around islets with hydrophobic marking pen
33. Fix cells with 75 microliters of 4% paraformaldehyde at room temperature for 10 minutes

49. Add 50 microliters of 5% formic acid for 15 minutes

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Prepare sterile instruments and reagents (scissors, forceps, DPBS in 35-ml culture dishes, 70% ethanol, gauze, paper towels)
2. Clean all surfaces of dissection area
3. Cover dissection area with clean paper towel
4. Place euthanized mouse on gauze in dissection area
5. Spray 70% ethanol on mouse's abdomen
6. Make lower midline abdominal incision with sterile dissection scissors to expose bladder
7. Grasp and gently pull up bladder with forceps to identify bilateral ureterovesical junction
8. Remove bladder fundus with scissors along boundary between ureter openings
9. Transfer bladder into sterile dish containing 2 milliliters of DPBS
10. Prepare sterile instruments and reagents
11. Transfer bladder to 35-millimeter dish in biosafety cabinet
12. Wash bladder with 2 milliliters of sterile DPBS
13. Collect bladder tissues from four mice into dish with 1 milliliter of complete culture medium without charcoal-stripped FBS
14. Mince each bladder into four equal pieces using surgical blade
15. Unfold minced bladder pieces with forceps to expose urothelium surface to medium
16. Transfer bladder pieces and medium into 15-milliliter centrifuge tube
17. Wash dish twice with 2 milliliters of complete culture medium without charcoal-stripped FBS
18. Add wash to centrifuge tube and adjust total volume to 5 milliliters
19. Add collagenase and hyaluronidase mixture to tube
20. Place tube horizontally in 37°C orbital shaker incubator at 200 RPM for 30 minutes
21. Add equal volume of 10% charcoal-stripped FBS and DPBS to digested tissue
22. Transfer mixture into tube
23. Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 minutes
24. Discard supernatant
25. Add 2 milliliters of trypsin substitute to cell pellet
26. Mix cell pellet and trypsin substitute thoroughly
27. Incubate tube at 37°C and 5% CO₂ for 4 minutes
28. Pipette cells up and down 10 times with standard P1000 tip
29. Add 5 milliliters of 10% charcoal-stripped FBS and DPBS
30. Strain dissociated cells through 100-micrometer sterile cell strainer and collect suspension in 50-milliliter tube
31. Transfer cell suspension to 15-milliliter tube
32. Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 minutes
33. Resuspend pellet in 1 milliliter of complete culture medium
34. Count cells using hemocytometer
35. Plate 500,000 cells per well in 24-well plate with 0.5 milliliters fresh complete culture medium
36. Add 2 microliters of adenovirus to 24-well plate
37. Mix adenovirus with dissociated urothelial cells
38. Centrifuge plate at 300g for 30 minutes (spinoculation)
39. Incubate plate at 37°C and 5% CO₂ for 1 hour
40. Transfer cells and medium from well to 15-mL tube
41. Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 minutes
42. Discard supernatant
43. Add 50 μL complete culture medium to cell pellet
44. Mix well to resuspend cells
45. Add 140 μL matrix extract to cell suspension
46. Gently mix to avoid air bubbles
47. Pipette 50 μL aliquots to create domes in prewarmed 6-well plate
48. Incubate plate for 5 minutes to solidify domes
49. Flip 6-well plate upside down
50. Continue solidification for 25 minutes
51. Add 2.5 milliliters of complete culture medium to each well
52. Place plate in incubator for organoid culture

21. Transfer lower lipid layers into one large glass vial using 25-milliliter glass serological pipette

30. Add 10 ml of protein solubilization buffer to protein interlayer tube

43. Divide supernatants into two 50-milliliter tubes
44. Add 7.5 milliliters of TCA to each tube using 10-milliliter glass serological pipette
45. Vortex samples into solution
46. Place samples in -20°C freezer for 2 hours to overnight

33. Swab insect injection surface with 95% ethanol
34. Inject 10 microliters of cell suspension into insect at <45° angle behind abdominal proleg
35. Plate 10⁻² to 10⁻⁶ dilutions on middle of agar plate
36. Let samples flow toward bottom of plate
37. Incubate plates at appropriate temperature
38. Count colonies to enumerate inoculum
39. Inject three to five insects with sterile PBS for negative control group
40. Incubate all insects at 26°C with 16-hour light/8-hour dark photoperiod
41. Monitor insect survival over time after injections
42. Inject insects with approximately 50 CFU of wild type or attenuated mutant strain of Xer Haus NLA grown to mid-log phase
43. Observe injected insects for approximately 72 hours

1. Seed fibroblasts into 24-well plates at 50,000 cells per well in 1 mL medium
2. Incubate plate overnight at 37°C and 5% CO₂
3. Prepare MMC media by mixing Ficoll 70, Ficoll 400, and ascorbic acid into 10% FCS DMEM
4. Incubate media in water bath to disperse crowders
5. Sterilize media using 0.2 micrometer filter
6. Aspirate spent media from fibroblasts
7. Replace aspirated media with freshly made MMC media
8. Incubate cells at 37°C for 6 days with MMC media changes every 3 days
9. Prepare Sirius Red solution by dissolving 0.2 grams of Direct Red 80 powder in 200 milliliters of distilled deionized water with one milliliter of acetic acid
10. Aspirate MMC media from cells
11. Add 300 microliters of Sirius Red solution to each well
12. Return cells to incubator for 90 minutes
13. Gently rinse Sirius Red solution with tap water
14. Allow plate to air dry overnight
15. Add 200 microliters of 0.1 molar sodium hydroxide to each well to extract Sirius Red
16. Shake plate for 5-10 minutes
17. Transfer 100 microliters of extracted stain to transparent 96-well plate
18. Measure absorbance at 620 nm using microplate reader
19. Wash each well with 200 microliters of PBS
20. Fix cells with methanol at 4°C for 10 minutes
21. Add 3% BSA to wells
22. Incubate plate for 30 minutes at room temperature
23. Aspirate blocking solution
24. Add 200 microliters of anti-collagen one antibody to each well
25. Incubate plate for 90 minutes
26. Aspirate antibody solution
27. Wash wells three times with PBS (5 minutes per wash)
28. Add 200 microliters of Goat Anti-Rabbit-FITC Secondary Antibody and DAPI to each well
29. Cover plate with aluminum foil and incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature
30. Discard secondary antibody and DAPI
31. Repeat PBS washes
32. Visualize fluorescence under microscope
33. Wash cells twice with PBS
34. Add 40 microliters of lysis buffer into each well
35. Scrape cell layer with pipette tip
36. Transfer protein lysate into microcentrifuge tubes
37. Load 10 micrograms of protein into each well of 4-12% Bis-Tris protein gel
38. Perform SDS-PAGE electrophoresis at 200 volts for 30 minutes
39. Transfer proteins to nitrocellulose membrane using western blot at 90 volts for 90 minutes while avoiding bubble formation between gel and membrane
40. Block membrane with 10 milliliters of blocking buffer
41. Incubate membrane with primary antibodies at 4°C overnight
42. Wash membrane five times with 0.1% TBS Tween 20 for 5 minutes per wash
43. Incubate membrane with species-appropriate secondary antibody for 1 hour at room temperature
44. Repeat washing procedure with 0.1% TBS Tween 20
45. Visualize fluorescence using imaging system
46. Measure RNA concentration using micro volume spectrophotometer
47. Prepare cDNA synthesis kit
48. Perform first strand DNA synthesis
49. Mix cDNA with 10 microliters of SYBR Green Supermix
50. Transfer mixture to custom 96-well plate pre-coated with oligonucleotide primers
51. Adjust total volume to 20 microliters per well with water
52. Run RT-PCR according to manuscript directions

43. Remove as much liquid as possible from testes
44. Apply 30-50 microliter drop of microscopy mounting medium to testes
45. Place 22 millimeter coverslip onto drop of mounting medium
46. Allow coverslip to settle and mounting medium to spread under coverslip

prompt:
Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Sort male and female mosquito pupae by size differences
2. Transfer 100 male pupae into pre-labeled cage
3. Transfer female pupae in batches of 40-50 per cage
4. Check cages for presence of male mosquitoes after adult emergence
5. Dissolve 200 milligrams of Rhodamine B powder in 100 milliliters of 10% sucrose solution
6. Mix solution thoroughly to ensure complete dissolution of powder
7. Prepare 20 sugar feeder bottles with wicks
8. Add 10 milliliters of 10% sucrose solution to 10 feeder bottles
9. Add 10 milliliters of 0.2% Rhodamine B sucrose solution to the remaining 10 feeder bottles
10. Place five feeder bottles into each prepared male cage
11. Allow male mosquitoes to feed from bottles for three days
12. Turn on mercury burner lamp
13. Turn on stereo microscope
14. Allow mercury burner lamp to stabilize for 10 minutes
15. Set fluorescence filters to red fluorescence protein one (RFP1)
16. Aspirate small number of mosquitoes into oral aspirator glass tube
17. Observe male mosquito bodies through glass tube under fluorescent stereo microscope to verify Rhodamine B marking
18. Transfer set A male mosquitoes: Place 10 sucrose-fed males per cup into six net-secured paper cups
19. Transfer set A male mosquitoes: Place 10 Rhodamine B sucrose-fed males per cup into six net-secured paper cups
20. Repeat transfer and grouping procedure for set B male mosquitoes
21. Set up 12 mating cages
22. Add mosquitoes to cages: For 6 cages - 10 Rhodamine B marked set A males, 10 unmarked set B males, 10 virgin wild-type females. For other 6 cages - 10 unmarked set A males, 10 Rhodamine B marked set B males, 10 virgin wild-type females
23. Label cages to distinguish mating combinations
24. Place respective male cups in mating cages according to labels
25. Remove netting and gently tap cup to release males
26. Allow male mosquitoes to acclimate in mating cage for at least 1 hour
27. Transfer virgin wild-type female mosquitoes into 12 paper cups using an oral aspirator
28. Transfer one cup of females into every mating cage and remove netting
29. Gently jostle cup to encourage remaining female mosquitoes out
30. Remove paper cup and netting from cage to prevent mosquito escapes
31. Allow mating to take place for three hours
32. Terminate mating experiment by removing all mosquitoes from each cage with mechanical aspirator
33. Cold-anesthetize mosquitoes on ice for at least five minutes
34. Gently pick up female mosquitoes and house them in separate netting-secured paper cup
35. Label paper cup by transferring respective label from mating cage
36. Cold-anesthetize female mosquitoes on ice for at least five minutes prior to dissection
37. Dissect female mosquito under stereo microscope
38. Examine spermathecae under microscope
39. Determine presence of Rhodamine B marked seminal fluid in spermathecae using fluorescent stereo microscope with RFP1 filter

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Add 1 mL of ice-cold 0.9% sodium chloride to 1.5-mL tube containing larvae
2. Close tube lid
3. Vertically flip tube to wash larvae
4. Place tube on ice for 30 seconds
5. Remove sodium chloride solution using 1-mL pipette
6. Centrifuge samples at 2,000 g for 1 minute at 4°C
7. Remove residual solution using 200-μL pipette and immediately freeze sample in liquid nitrogen
8. Label side of 2-mL screw-cap bead tube with ethanol-proof marker
9. Tare mass of labeled bead tube using analytical balance (0.01 mg accuracy)
10. Remove 1.5-mL sample tube from liquid nitrogen dewar using long forceps
11. Grab frozen tube while wearing nitrile gloves and invert it
12. Sharply pound inverted tube lid against benchtop to dislodge frozen pellet
13. Pour dislodged pellet into pre-tared 2-mL screw-cap bead tube
14. Measure combined mass of larval pellet and bead tube
15. Place sample tube into liquid nitrogen
16. Place sample tubes in -20°C benchtop cooler
17. Add 0.8 mL pre-chilled 90% methanol containing 2 μg/mL succinic-D4 acid to each sample tube
18. Return samples to -20°C benchtop cooler
19. Add 0.8 mL pre-chilled 90% methanol containing 2 μg/mL succinic-D4 acid to empty bead tube for negative control
20. Homogenize samples for 30 seconds at 6.45 meters per second using bead mill homogenizer in 4°C temperature control room
21. Return homogenized samples to -20°C benchtop cooler
22. Transfer cooler to -20°C freezer for at least one hour
23. Centrifuge tubes at 20,000 g for 5 minutes at 4°C to remove precipitate
24. Transfer 600 microliters of supernatant to new 1.5-milliliter microcentrifuge tube without disturbing precipitate
25. Open all sample tubes and place them in vacuum centrifuge
26. Dry samples at room temperature until all solvent is removed
27. Prepare solution of 40 mg/mL methoxylamine hydrochloride (MOX) in anhydrous pyridine
28. Store MOX and anhydrous pyridine in desiccator
29. Dry 1-mL glass syringe with heat gun for 5 seconds
30. Insert syringe needle into bottle of anhydrous pyridine
31. Withdraw 1 mL of anhydrous pyridine using syringe
32. Add withdrawn pyridine to microfuge tube containing 40 mg MOX
33. Flush bottle of anhydrous pyridine with argon
34. Seal the bottle
35. Return sealed bottle to desiccator
36. Dissolve MOX in pyridine by incubating in thermal mixer at 35°C for 10 minutes at 600 rpm
37. Add 40 microliters of 40 mg/mL MOX in anhydrous pyridine solution to dried sample
38. Vortex sample for 10 seconds
39. Centrifuge sample briefly
40. Incubate sample in thermal mixer
41. Centrifuge sample at 20,000 g or maximum speed for 5 minutes
42. Transfer 25 microliters of supernatant to autosampler vial with 250-microliter deactivated glass insert
43. Add 40 microliters of MSTFA containing 1% TMCS to vial
44. Place cap on autosampler vial
45. Seal vial using crimper tool
46. Incubate sample at 37°C for 1 hour with shaking at 250 rpm
47. Add 3 microliters of fatty acid methyl ester (FAMES) standard solution to vial using robotic autosampler

Question: Given the complete step list of the experiment, please predict the next step that will take place after experimental steps shown in this video.
Complete step list: Place pre-prepared mold in aluminum foil-covered glass Petri dish
2. Prepare 30-40 ml PDMS mixture by weighing 1:10 ratio of curing agent to elastomer
3. Mix PDMS continuously for approximately 5 minutes until mixture appears white and nearly opaque
4. Pour PDMS mixture into Petri dish containing mold
5. Degas PDMS in desiccator until no bubbles remain
6. Bake mold with liquid PDMS in oven or on hot plate at 70°C until rubber-like consistency is obtained
7. Cut device out by tracing around features with scalpel while pushing forward (not down) due to mold fragility
8. Remove cutout PDMS device from mold
9. Place PDMS device upside down in new Petri dish
10. Punch holes in device using blunt 20-gauge syringe needle based on imprinted pattern
11. Insert cleaned PDMS and coverslip into plasma cleaner
12. Close plasma cleaner valves and turn on power, vacuum, and pump
13. Run plasma cleaner for approximately 1 minute
14. Set RF to high and allow controlled air entry using fine valve
15. Monitor viewing window until color changes from purple to pink, then run plasma cleaner for 50 seconds and turn RF off
16. Maintain pump operation for 1 minute after RF deactivation
17. Gradually open main valve to reintroduce air into plasma cleaner
18. Press PDMS surface onto cleaned coverslip for bonding
19. Confirm bond integrity by testing for detachment when pulling coverslip slightly
20. Secure 90-degree blunt needle with pliers
21. Insert one end of needle into Tygon tube
22. Insert other end of needle into punched hole of device
23. Repeat needle-tubing assembly process for remaining device holes
24. Apply small amount of immersion oil to surface of copper cold stage
25. Spread oil using lint-free wipe to create thin layer
26. Place clean sapphire disc on created oil layer
27. Apply droplet of immersion oil onto center of sapphire disc
28. Position PDMS device onto oil droplet with features aligned over viewing hole of cold stage
29. Secure tubing to outer walls of aluminum box housing adhesive tape
30. Inject 4-5 microliters of antifreeze protein solution into inlet channel using glass syringe
31. Close lid of cold stage
32. Initiate temperature control program
33. Set temperature to -25°C
34. Increase temperature gradually at rate of 1°C per 5 seconds toward sample melting point
35. Switch microscope to 10x or 20x objective
36. Grow single crystal by slightly decreasing temperature until crystal ends meet channel walls
37. Switch microscope to 50x objective
38. Inject antifreeze protein solution into channels and observe fluorescence intensity increase
39. Slowly inject buffer solution into second inlet of microfluidic device
40. Observe decrease in fluorescent signal using NIS-Elements Imaging Program
41. Inject THF-water solution (1:15 molar ratio) into microfluidic device
42. Slowly increase temperature until all ice melts while preserving hydrates
43. Hold temperature at 1°C for 3 minutes
44. Set temperature to -2°C
45. Observe hydrate abundance in microfluidic channels under inhibitor-free conditions
46. Inject antifreeze protein or inhibitor into microfluidic channel using glass syringe
47. Adjust temperature to maintain crystal stability
48. Allow inhibitor molecules to adsorb to crystal surface for several minutes
49. Perform solution exchange by injecting inhibitor-free solution into channel
50. Capture images of crystal before and after solution exchange
51. Analyze fluorescence intensity on crystal and in solution using imaging program
52. Form and isolate a single crystal in microfluidic channels
53. Exchange solution around the isolated crystal

1. Place eight-day-old specific pathogen-free embryonated chicken eggs in rotating egg tray with stamped ends facing upward

3. Incubate eggs for 48 hours
4. Place incubated eggs in egg rack with stamped ends up
5. Transfer egg rack to laminar flow hood
6. Turn off room and hood lights
7. Hold stamped end of egg lightly to egg candler to expose vasculature of chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) and air sack
8. Make a mark between two major blood vessels with a pencil
9. Make a hole at egg tip above air sack at stamped end using sterile push pin (3mm deep)
10. Make a second hole at pencil mark using sterile push pin (3mm deep)
11. Squeeze air from safety bulb
12. Press safety bulb firmly against hole above air sack
13. Slowly release bulb to apply suction at pencil mark hole
14. Confirm air sack displacement to pencil mark using candler
15. Make both holes deeper if air sack displacement unsuccessful
16. Deepen both holes slightly
17. Reapply suction using safety bulb
18. Hold egg with one hand and position rotary tool with 1.5-1.6 inch cutoff wheel attachment
19. Make two transverse cuts (2 cm length, 1 cm apart) through shell without touching CAM
20. Make longitudinal cuts at ends of transverse cuts by lightly touching cutoff wheel to shell
21. Slide sterile forceps under and parallel to shell piece
22. Grab shell piece with forceps and cleanly remove it
23. Place basement membrane protein mixture (e.g., matrigel) on ice to prevent polymerization
24. Use 4-5 ml of 2 mM EDTA solution per flask to detach tumor cells
25. Place flask in tissue culture incubator for 5 minutes
26. Resuspend detached cells in medium
27. Count cell number
28. Transfer volume required for 500,000-2 million cells to new tube
29. Centrifuge tube at 500 × g for 5 minutes
30. Discard supernatant
31. Resuspend cell pellet in 40 μl PBS containing calcium
32. Peel tape off the egg
33. Drop sterile 1 mm silicone ring from cryogenic vial through opening onto CAM
34. Pipette 60 microliter solution of cells, PBS plus plus, and basement membrane mixture into center of silicone ring
35. Retape the egg window
36. Carefully move egg tray back to incubator
37. Allow tumors to grow for 5-7 days
38. Place underpad and biohazard bag in hood
39. Prepare 35 mm × 10 mm plates containing 1 ml PBS plus plus and paraformaldehyde containers
40. Insert pointed end of sterile dissection scissors into egg at hole near stamped end and cut around length of entire egg
41. Extract tumor from CAM using dissection scissors and forceps
42. Place tumor in 35 mm × 10 mm plate
43. Measure and weigh tumor
44. Fix tumor in paraformaldehyde for paraffin embedding
45. Mince harvested tumor in plate using dissection scissors
46. Transfer minced tumor to 15 mL centrifuge tube
47. Remove PBS plus plus from tube by pipetting
48. Add 2 mL of 1 mg/mL collagenase solution in PBS plus plus
49. Mix solution by inverting tube several times
50. Incubate tube at 37°C for 30 minutes to several hours
51. Add 5 mL medium to tube and mix by pipetting 20-40 times
52. Transfer supernatant to fresh tube after sedimentation
53. Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes and discard supernatant

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Dissect 6-8 hippocampi from postnatal day 1 pups using HBSS medium in Petri dish
2. Chop hippocampi into smaller pieces using dissection scissors
3. Transfer chopped hippocampi from Petri dish to 15 mL tube
4. Wash hippocampi twice with 5 mL HBSS
5. Leave hippocampi in 4.5 mL HBSS after washing
6. Add 0.5 mL of 2.5% trypsin to 4.5 mL HBSS containing hippocampi
7. Incubate tube in 37°C water bath for 15 minutes with inversion every 5 minutes
8. Wash hippocampi with HBSS three times for five minutes per wash
9. Add two milliliters of HBSS to hippocampi
10. Pipette hippocampi up and down 15 times with Pasteur pipette
11. Triturate tissue 10 times with fire-polished Pasteur pipette
12. Rest tube for five minutes until chunks settle to bottom
13. Repeat trituration with remaining chunks until most disappear
14. Transfer supernatant containing dissociated neurons to plating dishes using one milliliter pipette tip
15. Add culture directly to pre-incubated plating medium
16. Shake plate gently
17. Check plating dishes with light microscope 2-4 hours after seeding
18. Use fine tip forceps to flip cover slips
19. Transfer cover slips to glial cell feeder dishes containing preconditioned neuronal culture medium
20. Position cover slips with wax dots side facing downwards
21. Feed neurons with 1 mL fresh neuronal culture medium every 7 days
22. Flip cover slips on third day in vitro
23. Position cover slips with wax dot side facing up in glial cell feeder dish with conditioned medium
24. Mix 0.25 micrograms of CRE-BFP DNA with 0.5 micrograms of ankyrin-G GFP DNA in a 1.7 milliliter tube
25. Add 100 microliters of optimum to the DNA mixture tube
26. Mix the DNA-optimum tube and rest it on a rack
27. Mix 3 microliters of transfection reagent with 100 microliters of optimum in a new 1.7 milliliter tube
28. Incubate transfection reagent mixture for 5 minutes at room temperature
29. Mix 100 microliters of DNA mixture with 100 microliters of transfection reagent mixture
30. Leave mixture for 5-10 minutes on a rack
31. Add 50 microliters of DNA mix on top of each cover slip by inserting pipette tip below medium without touching cover slips while pipetting slowly
32. Transfer dish slowly to incubator
33. Incubate dish for 30-45 minutes
34. Flip cover slips onto home glial feeder dish with wax dot side facing down
35. Return dish to incubator
36. Open Z series images in Fiji
37. Generate maximum projection of images
38. Subtract empty cover slip background signal from image
39. Draw line along AIS with width fully covering the structure, starting before signal rise and stopping after signal drop
40. Measure mean pixel intensity along the line
41. Export intensity data to spreadsheet
42. Run MATLAB script to generate final figure

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Add 20 microliters of freshly prepared POPC solution and 4 microliters of freshly prepared biotin-PEG-DSPE solution to a glass vial
2. Evaporate organic solvent by air flow until lipid film forms
3. Place lipid film in desiccator for one hour to completely evaporate organic solvent
4. Add 200 microliters of mineral oil to the vial
5. Cover vial opening with plastic paraffin film
6. Sonicate vial contents in ultrasonic bath at 120 watts for at least one hour
7. Create a lipid film
8. Add 200 microliters of 200 millimolar glucose in LB medium to the lipid film
9. Sonicate the film at 120 watts for at least one hour
10. Extrude resulting giant vesicles into small vesicles using a mini extruder and polycarbonate membrane with 100-nanometer pore size
11. Inoculate E. coli from LB plate into LB medium
12. Incubate culture overnight at 37°C
13. Transfer 20 microliters of culture supernatant to 1.98 milliliters of fresh LB medium
14. Incubate sub-culture for two hours
15. Measure optical density at 600 nm (OD600) using spectrophotometer
16. Mix pre-culture solution with sucrose solution and fresh LB medium according to table one
17. Add 50 microliters of freshly prepared outer aqueous solution to a 1.5 milliliter lidded plastic tube
18. Layer 150 microliters of lipid-containing oil solution over the outer aqueous solution
19. Incubate solution for 10 to 15 minutes at room temperature
20. Verify oil-aqueous solution interface is flat
21. Add 2 microliters of freshly prepared inner aqueous solution of giant vesicles to 50 microliters of sonicated lipid-containing oil solution in 0.6 milliliter lidded plastic tube
22. Tap tube to emulsify components
23. Use pipette to add 50 microliters of water and oil droplet solution to oil-aqueous solution interface
24. Sediment bacterial cell-containing giant vesicles by centrifugation
25. Aspirate top oil layer
26. Collect giant vesicles
27. Drill a seven-millimeter hole with hollow punch on 10x10x1 mm double-faced seal
28. Paste double-faced seal onto 30x40 mm cover glass
29. Add 30 microliters of small vesicle solution to chamber hole
30. Incubate vesicles at room temperature for 30 minutes
31. Gently wash chamber hole twice with 20 microliters LB medium supplemented with 200 mM glucose
32. Introduce 10 microliters of neutravidin in outer aqueous giant vesicle solution to the hole
33. Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature
34. Gently wash the hole two times with 20 microliters of LB medium supplemented with 200 mM glucose
35. Add entire volume of giant vesicle solution to the hole in the chamber
36. Seal the hole with 18 × 18 millimeter cover glass
37. Select 40X objective on inverted microscope
38. Place chamber on microscope heating stage system
39. Incubate bacterial cell-containing giant vesicles in chamber under static conditions at 37°C for six hours
40. Capture and record images of bacterial cell growth every 30 minutes using scientific complementary metal oxide semiconductor camera
41. Aspirate oil carefully before giant vesicle correction

8. Separate spinal cord from body
9. Pinch rostrad part of spinal cord

52. Withdraw 100 microliters of culture medium from target well

13. Mix solution by pipetting up and down

1. Shave the surgical knee with electric clippers

7. Open knee joint by medial para patella arthrotomy under sterile conditions
8. Displace the patella
9. Displace patella laterally

12. Rinse defects with sterile saline
13. Use forceps to remove residual cartilage pieces

4. Pick single gravid adult from fourth chunk plate

33. Add 200 µl of 1 mg/ml E. coli and 1:50 dilution of 0.5 µM red fluorescent microsphere solution to worm suspension
34. Incubate at room temperature with rocking for 20 minutes
35. Collect worms and microspheres by centrifugation
36. Wash worms twice with fresh M9 solution to remove excess bacteria and uninternalized microspheres
37. Resuspend pellet in 5 ml M9 solution after second wash

39. Place tube on rocker to straighten and euthanize worms
40. Open calibrated 384-well plate template
41. Set template to dispense 20 gated objects into four wells
42. Load 40 milliliter sample of worms onto large particle flow cytometer
43. Begin automatic sorting of sample
44. Continuously stir sample to prevent settling
45. Dispense objects from sample into calibrated 384-well plate
46. Remove sample from cytometer
47. Clean instrument

30. Remove primary blocking solution

34. Remove secondary blocking solution
35. Add freshly prepared primary antibody solution

40. Rinse slides with 400 microliters of immunofluorescence buffer for 20 minutes

43. Wash slides thrice with 400 microliters of PBS
44. Pipette out entire PBS from wells
45. Ensure removal of residual solution
46. Add one drop of mounting reagent into each well
47. Allow slides to stand at room temperature overnight

prompt:
Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Calibrate probe sonicator fitted with vial block sonitrobe
2. Measure 2 mg of chosen nanopowder into each of three clean 10 or 20 mL glass vials (numbered 1-3) using clean metal spatula
3. Pipette 1 mL deionized water along inner walls of each vial
4. For hydrophobic samples: Pipette 1 mL of 0.5% (v/v) ethanol in deionized water along inner walls
5. Mix each sample into thick paste
6. Add sufficient deionized water to paste to achieve final concentration of 0.2 mg/mL
7. Horizontally swirl vials to dislodge nanopowder adhering to inner walls
8. Transfer 1.5 milliliters of each nanopowder dispersion to clean labeled microcentrifuge tubes
9. Firmly close microcentrifuge tubes
10. Swirl closed tubes to dislodge nanopowder from inner walls
11. Place samples in sonitrobe
12. Sonicate samples at 1.1 watts
13. Sonicate samples at 1.1 watts with pulse setting (1 second on, 1 second off) for 2 minutes
14. Remove sample one from sonication block
15. Transfer 1 milliliter from top of dispersion to clean microcentrifuge tube
16. Add deionized water to attain sample concentration of 0.02 mg/mL
17. Immediately begin sample characterization
18. Sonicate remaining samples for four minutes
19. Maintain same amplitude and pulse settings during sonication
20. Dilute sample two to 0.02 mg/mL with deionized water
21. Begin characterization of sample two
22. Sonicate sample three for four minutes
23. Maintain same amplitude and pulse settings during sonication
24. Dilute sample three to 0.02 mg/mL
25. Begin characterization of sample three
26. Calibrate ultrasonic bath with respect to bath sensor
27. Place 2 milligrams of nanopowder in each of four clean glass vials using clean spatula
28. Number vials four through seven
29. Pipette 1 milliliter of deionized water along vial walls and mix into thick paste
30. Add deionized water to achieve 0.2 milligrams per milliliter concentration in each vial
31. Cap vials and swirl to dislodge nanopowder adhering to inner surfaces
32. Place vials in center of calibrated ultrasonic bath
33. Ensure water level is halfway up the vials
34. Sonicate sample at 80 watts for 15 minutes at room temperature
35. Transfer aliquot of sample four to clean vial
36. Dilute aliquot with deionized water to 0.02 milligrams per milliliter
37. Begin characterization of diluted sample
38. Replace ultrasonic bath water with fresh room temperature water
39. Open dynamic light scattering instrument software
40. Create size measurement file
41. Configure parameters: equilibration time, temperature, cuvette type, experiment mode
42. Save size measurement file
43. Run DLS verification measurement using standard 100nm latex beads
44. Confirm instrument performance meets standards
45. Slowly pipette 1 mL of dilute nanopowder dispersion into clean low-volume disposable cuvette while avoiding air bubbles
46. Insert cuvette into instrument
47. Start data collection
48. Take at least five measurements per sample
49. Select all measurements
50. Calculate average for each sample
51. Export measurement data to spreadsheet program for analysis
52. Open UV-Vis instrument software and initialize new measurement
53. Pipette 2-3 milliliters of dilute nanopowder dispersion into clean standard quartz cuvette
54. Set instrument wavelength range to 700 nanometers to 200 nanometers
55. Acquire solvent blank spectrum for background subtraction
56. Acquire at least three sample spectra
57. Export spectral data for further analysis
58. Place drop of dilute nanopowder dispersion on 300 mesh holey carbon film
59. Allow sample to air-dry under ambient conditions while protected from airborne contamination
60. Wash grid with ultra pure water to remove effects from uneven drying
61. Acquire TEM images and export them for further analysis

1. Place pre-prepared mold in aluminum foil-covered glass Petri dish
2. Prepare 30-40 ml PDMS mixture by weighing 1:10 ratio of curing agent to elastomer
3. Mix PDMS continuously for approximately 5 minutes until mixture appears white and nearly opaque
4. Pour PDMS mixture into Petri dish containing mold
5. Degas PDMS in desiccator until no bubbles remain
6. Bake mold with liquid PDMS in oven or on hot plate at 70°C until rubber-like consistency is obtained
7. Cut device out by tracing around features with scalpel while pushing forward (not down) due to mold fragility
8. Remove cutout PDMS device from mold
9. Place PDMS device upside down in new Petri dish
10. Punch holes in device using blunt 20-gauge syringe needle based on imprinted pattern
11. Insert cleaned PDMS and coverslip into plasma cleaner
12. Close plasma cleaner valves and turn on power, vacuum, and pump
13. Run plasma cleaner for approximately 1 minute
14. Set RF to high and allow controlled air entry using fine valve
15. Monitor viewing window until color changes from purple to pink, then run plasma cleaner for 50 seconds and turn RF off
16. Maintain pump operation for 1 minute after RF deactivation
17. Gradually open main valve to reintroduce air into plasma cleaner
18. Press PDMS surface onto cleaned coverslip for bonding
19. Confirm bond integrity by testing for detachment when pulling coverslip slightly
20. Secure 90-degree blunt needle with pliers
21. Insert one end of needle into Tygon tube
22. Insert other end of needle into punched hole of device
23. Repeat needle-tubing assembly process for remaining device holes
24. Apply small amount of immersion oil to surface of copper cold stage
25. Spread oil using lint-free wipe to create thin layer
26. Place clean sapphire disc on created oil layer
27. Apply droplet of immersion oil onto center of sapphire disc
28. Position PDMS device onto oil droplet with features aligned over viewing hole of cold stage
29. Secure tubing to outer walls of aluminum box housing adhesive tape
30. Inject 4-5 microliters of antifreeze protein solution into inlet channel using glass syringe
31. Close lid of cold stage
32. Initiate temperature control program
33. Set temperature to -25°C
34. Increase temperature gradually at rate of 1°C per 5 seconds toward sample melting point
35. Switch microscope to 10x or 20x objective
36. Grow single crystal by slightly decreasing temperature until crystal ends meet channel walls
37. Switch microscope to 50x objective
38. Inject antifreeze protein solution into channels and observe fluorescence intensity increase
39. Slowly inject buffer solution into second inlet of microfluidic device
40. Observe decrease in fluorescent signal using NIS-Elements Imaging Program
41. Inject THF-water solution (1:15 molar ratio) into microfluidic device
42. Slowly increase temperature until all ice melts while preserving hydrates
43. Hold temperature at 1°C for 3 minutes
44. Set temperature to -2°C
45. Observe hydrate abundance in microfluidic channels under inhibitor-free conditions
46. Inject antifreeze protein or inhibitor into microfluidic channel using glass syringe
47. Adjust temperature to maintain crystal stability
48. Allow inhibitor molecules to adsorb to crystal surface for several minutes
49. Perform solution exchange by injecting inhibitor-free solution into channel
50. Capture images of crystal before and after solution exchange
51. Analyze fluorescence intensity on crystal and in solution using imaging program
52. Form and isolate a single crystal in microfluidic channels
53. Exchange solution around the isolated crystal

1. Culture HCT116 cell line in DMEM cell culture medium

4. Add three milliliters of ice-cold PBS supplemented with five-millimolar EDTA
5. Incubate plates for five minutes at room temperature
6. Detach cells from plates using a cell scraper
7. Collect cells in 50-milliliter tube placed on ice
8. Centrifuge at 250 G for 10 minutes
9. Measure volume of harvested cells using tube's volumetric scale
10. Resuspend harvested cell pellet in equal volume of lysis buffer
11. Lyse cells by sonication
12. Spin sample at 100,000 G for one hour at 4°C in ultracentrifuge rotor
13. Remove cleared lysate using syringe without disturbing pellet or floating layer
14. Add 2 microliters of cleared lysate into tube
15. Add 18 microliters of water to tube
16. Add 5 microliters of 5X SDS sample buffer to tube
17. Add 1 mM GTP and 20 µM paclitaxel to collected supernatant
18. Incubate mixture at 37°C for 30 minutes
19. Prepare cushion buffer by adding 600 µL glycerol to 400 µL lysis buffer
20. Supplement cushion buffer with 20 µM paclitaxel
21. Prewarm cushion buffer to 37°C
22. Add 800 microliters of cushion buffer to an ultracentrifuge tube
23. Pipette GTP-paclitaxel-supplemented lysate carefully on top of cushion buffer
24. Place tube in ultracentrifuge rotor
25. Centrifuge at 100,000 G at 30°C for 30 minutes
26. Mark outward-facing edge of tube to identify microtubule pellet location
27. Add lysis buffer next to pellet
28. Rotate tube several times to remove glycerol from pellet and tube walls
29. Aspirate and repeat glycerol washing step three times
30. Resuspend washed pellet gently using cut pipette tip in 50 microliters prewarmed resuspension buffer
31. Place tube at 37 degrees Celsius
32. Install blotting paper in plunge freezer device
33. Set plunge freezer temperature to 30 degrees Celsius
34. Set plunge freezer humidification to 100%
35. Allow device to equilibrate for 30 minutes
36. Configure plunge freezer for two applications
37. Set first application parameters: force=10, blot time=2 seconds, wait time=0 seconds
38. Place EM grids with carbon side up into metal glow discharger vehicle
39. Glow discharge EM grids at 30 milliamperes for 60 seconds
40. Cool polystyrene container assembly with liquid nitrogen
41. Prepare liquid ethane by condensing ethane gas into cold metal cup
42. Grab glow discharged grid with plunge tweezers
43. Click grid into plunge freezer
44. Position polystyrene container with liquid ethane in plunge freezer
45. Run through prepared program
46. Apply 3.5 microliters of microtubule solution to grid
47. Let plunge freezer blot grid
48. Apply 3.5 microliters of diluted protein
49. Let plunger blot and plunge freeze grid in liquid ethane

1. Thaw matrigel aliquot on ice at 4°C

3. Mix gel components on ice in specified sequence
4. Incubate final gel solution at 4°C for 1 hour

6. Count cells
7. Resuspend cells in serum-free media at 5×10⁶ cells/mL concentration

9. Mix cell-gel solution thoroughly by pipetting gently up and down

13. Add 1,200 microliters of serum-free media under insert for static condition

16. Avoid creating air bubbles beneath insert during flow condition setup

32. Place plate on shaker at 150 RPM for 30 minutes at room temperature

36. Place membranes on glass slides with transmigrated cells facing up

19. Serially dilute 40 microliters of polydopamine-coated nanodiamonds suspension twice with deionized water

27. Discard supernatant

30. Redisperse nanodiamonds by sonication for 30 seconds
31. Redisperse samples by sonication for 30 seconds
32. Characterize nanodiamonds with UV-Vis spectroscopy scanning from 250 to 550 nanometers
33. Deposit 5 microliters of silver nanoparticle-decorated nanodiamonds on plasma-cleaned carbon-coated copper grids
34. Let grids sit for 3 minutes
35. Wick away excess solution with filter paper
36. Apply drop of deionized water to each grid
37. Let water sit on grid for 15 seconds
38. Wick away water with filter paper

11. Wash particles with 3-5 cycles of centrifugation and resuspension in fresh exchange buffer
12. Concentrate particle mixture to approximately 5 microliters for 20 mg/mL particle loading
13. Clean silicone internal reflection element by low power sonication in sulfuric acid for 15 minutes
14. Continue cleaning by sonication in nitric acid for one hour
15. Rinse element in ultrapure water
16. Dry element under stream of dry nitrogen gas
17. Apply electrical grade silicone sealant to fix IRE into baseplate of five reflection ATR accessory, keeping sealant to edges
18. Allow sealant to dry completely
19. Transfer baseplate into dry anaerobic glove box
20. Mount baseplate on ATR accessory
21. Acquire background infrared spectrum in rapid scan mode
22. Detach ATR accessory baseplate
23. Transfer baseplate to wet anaerobic glove box
24. Dropcast 1 microliter of enzyme-modified carbon black particles evenly over IRE surface without allowing particles to dry

26. Mount custom spectroelectrochemical cell over IRE
27. Add 200 microliters of experiment buffer via solution inlet
28. Connect solution inlet and outlet to experiment buffer vial via peristaltic pump tubing
29. Transfer assembled cell to dry glove box
30. Mount cell assembly on ATR accessory
31. Connect tubing to peristaltic pump
32. Acquire absorption spectrum using previously acquired spectrum as background
33. Verify MI2 bands are strongly visible at 1,540 cm⁻¹
34. Verify hydrogenase active site peaks are detectable in 1,850-2,150 cm⁻¹ region
35. Apply reducing potential of -0.8 V vs. saturated calomel reference electrode to particle film
36. Saturate experiment buffer with anaerobic hydrogen gas
37. Initiate flow of hydrogen-saturated buffer through spectroelectrochemical cell at 12 mL/min
38. Maintain sample under flowing hydrogen-saturated buffer overnight for hydrogenase activation
39. Acquire absorption spectrum of activated sample
40. Saturate experiment buffer with anaerobic nitrogen gas
41. Flow nitrogen-saturated buffer through the cell
42. Apply oxidizing potential of 0 V vs. saturated calomel reference electrode

44. Acquire absorption spectrum during oxidation
45. Apply reducing potential for 30 minutes

48. Check electrical connections of the cell
49. Acquire cyclic voltammograms using anaerobic hydrogen saturated buffer at increasing flow rates

3. Inject argon gas into system at 40 mL/min

5. Ignite plasma and set power output to 40 W

12. Position sulfur boat 2 cm upstream of heating zone to achieve 120°C at 800°C substrate temperature
13. Close furnace and pump down to 5 × 10⁻³ torr
14. Flow argon gas through furnace at 130 mL/min
15. Stabilize furnace pressure at 0.7 torr
16. Ramp furnace temperature from room temperature to 800°C at 20°C/min
17. Hold furnace at 800°C until sulfur fully evaporates
18. Turn off furnace heat and cool substrate to room temperature under argon flow
