20. Sputter tungsten on substrate for 30 seconds using same settings as for molybdenum
21. Place tungsten-coated substrate in center of furnace heating zone
22. Place one gram of sulfur powder two centimeters upstream of heating zone
23. Sulfurize tungsten film using same parameters as for molybdenum film

28. Prepare tweezers with round, flat tips
29. Carefully peel one corner of PMMA with attached TMD film from substrate

35. Obtain 300 nm thick P-type silicon dioxide on silicon substrate patterned with titanium or gold electrodes
36. Immerse patterned substrate in deionized water and attach TMD film to substrate
37. Bake substrate with attached film at 100 degrees Celsius for 3 minutes to evaporate water
38. Cover substrate surface with PMMA to secure film attachment
39. Dry substrate in electronic drying cabinet for eight hours
40. Remove PMMA layer from substrate
41. Fabricate TMD heterostructure transistor using photolithography and reactive ion etching

prompt:
Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Harvest human endothelial EAHY 926 cells at 95% confluency
2. Wash cells with 10 milliliters of PBS to remove growth media
3. Incubate cells in trypsin-EDTA solution for detachment
4. Transfer detached cells to conical tube
5. Centrifuge cells
6. Resuspend cells in 25 ml of complete DMEM medium at 1 million cells/ml concentration
7. Place one Thermon cover slip in each well of 24-well tissue culture plate using sterile forceps
8. Orient cover slip with opaque/cell-adherent side facing upwards
9. Add 500 microliters of cell suspension to each well
10. Incubate plate at 37°C for 48 hours or until cells reach confluency
11. Use clean forceps to remove each cover slip
12. Dip cover slips in DMEM to remove soluble secreted proteins
13. Transfer washed cover slips to individual wells of fresh 24-well plate containing 490 microliters per well of complete DMEM while maintaining orientation (cells facing upward)
14. Prepare 10 milliliter culture of Staphylococcus aureus in brain heart infusion broth
15. Transfer bacterial culture into conical tube
16. Centrifuge bacteria at 5,000 times G for 10 minutes
17. Remove supernatant after pelleting cells
18. Resuspend pellet in 10 milliliters of sterile DMEM
19. Centrifuge cells again to repeat wash
20. Perform wash procedure three times total
21. Resuspend bacteria in DMEM after final wash
22. Measure optical density of bacterial suspension
23. Adjust concentration to obtain OD600 of 1.0 (approximately 10^9 CFU/mL)
24. Add 10 microliters of bacterial suspension to each well of 24-well plate containing cover slips
25. Incubate plate at 37 degrees Celsius for 15-90 minutes to allow bacterial attachment and invasion
26. Aspirate supernatant from each well and replace with 10% FBS-DMEM supplemented with Gentamycin
27. Incubate plate at 37 degrees Celsius for 60 minutes to kill extracellular bacteria
28. Wash each cover slip in DMEM three times to remove antibiotic
29. Transfer cover slips to new 24-well plate containing 500 microliters of 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS per well
30. Maintain cover slips with cell-covered side facing up during transfer
31. Vigorously rinse each cover slip by pipetting Triton solution up and down directly onto cover slip to lyse cells and release intracellular bacteria
32. Perform serial dilutions of the lysate to quantify infecting bacteria
33. Collect lysate and plate serial dilutions on TSA plates

4. Dry glass plates with tissue and air blower
5. Place glass plates in UV ozone photoreactor
6. Treat glass plates in UV ozone photoreactor for 20 minutes to remove organic residues

8. Place glass plate on spin coater

18. Mix UV curing glue with 20μm diameter glass beads
19. Place two glue drops at adjacent corners of planar-aligned glass plate
20. Place two additional glue drops 5mm from other corners
21. Assemble homeotropic-aligned plate atop first plate with 4mm edge gap
22. UV cure assembly for 2 minutes
23. Place cell on hot plate with homeotropic side upwards
24. Set hot plate temperature to 110 degrees Celsius
25. Place LC mixture on edge of cell to melt solid and initiate capillary flow
26. Add more LC mixture at edge until cell is fully filled
27. Slowly cool cell to 90 degrees Celsius to reach nematic phase

35. Cut a strip along the molecular director of the film
36. Clamp film sample using self-closing tweezers
37. Position clamped sample to allow 1.7 centimeters of film free to move
38. Hold sample vertically
39. Direct LED beam perpendicular to sample for self-oscillation observation
40. Observe film attached to glass substrate between crossed polarizers above diffused white light source to verify splay alignment

12. Coat four wells of 12-well plate with 0.1 milligrams per milliliter collagen in 50 millimolar acetic acid
13. Allow collagen to adhere to wells at room temperature for one hour

17. Discard supernatant
18. Add 10 milliliters of sterile 25% w/v BSA in PBS to tissue
19. Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 20 minutes at 4°C
20. Carefully discard supernatant
21. Discard supernatant after centrifugation
22. Dissolve pellet in 15 milliliters of buffer A

39. Remove supernatant-polybrene mixture from wells

43. Transfer stable cell lines to collagen-coated tissue culture flasks

46. Add 5 milliliters of medium to flask
47. Seed cells into new flasks at ≤1:4 split ratio

50. Resuspend cell pellet in 6 ml of freezing medium

52. Place cryo vials into Nalgene freezing container filled with isopropanol
53. Store cryo vials at -80°C for one day
54. Transfer cryo vials to long-term storage under liquid nitrogen vapor

Complete step list: Grow bacteria in 5 ml LB broth with 10 mM calcium chloride and optionally 25 μg/ml kanamycin to OD600=1.0
2. Prepare dilution series of P1 phage stock in LB medium
3. Mix 200 μl bacterial suspension with 100 μl of each phage dilution in 15 ml centrifuge tubes
4. Incubate tubes statically for 20 minutes at 37 degrees Celsius
5. Add approximately three milliliters of molten top agar supplemented with ten millimolar calcium chloride to tubes
6. Mix tube contents by vortexing
7. Pour mixtures onto pre-warmed LB plates to make even layers
8. Incubate plates overnight at 37 degrees Celsius
9. Select plate with semi-confluent growth of phage plaques
10. Scrape top agar layer using inoculation loop
11. Transfer scraped agar to centrifuge tube
12. Add 1-2 mL LB to tube under fume hood
13. Add one drop chloroform to tube
14. Vortex tube vigorously for one minute
15. Centrifuge to pellet agar and bacterial cells
16. Transfer supernatant to microcentrifuge tube while avoiding pellet debris
17. Add two drops chloroform to supernatant
18. Store lysate at 4-10 degrees Celsius
19. Grow recipient strain in LB to optical density of 1 at 600 nm
20. Add calcium chloride to recipient strain culture to 10 millimolar concentration with mixing
21. Add appropriate volume of phage lysate (taken from sample top to avoid chloroform transfer) to 1 ml recipient culture to achieve multiplicity of infection of 0.5
22. Statically incubate mixture for 20 minutes at 37 degrees Celsius
23. Add sodium citrate to reach 100 millimoles per liter concentration to stop infection
24. Centrifuge transduced bacteria
25. Resuspend pellet in 1 milliliter of fresh LB supplemented with 100 millimolar sodium citrate
26. Wash cells twice with LB supplemented with 100 millimolar sodium citrate to remove free phages and calcium
27. Resuspend washed bacteria in 1 mL fresh LB supplemented with 100 mM sodium citrate
28. Incubate resuspended bacteria at 30°C with 100 RPM shaking for 1 hour
29. Collect bacteria by centrifugation
30. Resuspend pellet in approximately 100 μL LB supplemented with 100 mM sodium citrate
31. Spread bacteria on LB plate supplemented with 25 μg/mL kanamycin and 10 mM sodium citrate
32. Incubate plate at 30°C until colonies appear
33. Restreak colonies onto new LB agar plates supplemented with kanamycin
34. Incubate plates at 30°C until single colonies appear
35. Prepare electrocompetent cells from kanamycin-resistant recipient strain
36. Add 1 picogram of pCP20 plasmid DNA to cell suspension
37. Gently mix DNA-cell suspension
38. Transfer mixture to pre-cooled 1 mm electroporation cuvette
39. Set electroporator to 1.8 kilovolts
40. Perform electroporation
41. Rescue transformed cells with 1 ml SOC medium
42. Incubate rescued cells at 30°C for 1 hour
43. Plate 100 microliters of cells on LB plus ampicillin plates
44. Incubate plates overnight at 30 degrees Celsius
45. Pick single colonies and inoculate in fresh LB without antibiotics
46. Grow inoculated cells overnight at 43 degrees Celsius to induce flippase recombinase expression
47. Plate 50 microliter serial dilutions on non-selective plates
48. Incubate serial dilution plates overnight at 30 degrees Celsius

prompt:
Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Transfer individual Stentor cells into well of glass spot plate containing at least 100 microliters of commercially available pasteurized spring water using one milliliter pipette
2. Transfer 1 milliliter aliquot from Chlamydomonas culture into 1.5 milliliter microcentrifuge tube
3. Centrifuge sample at 2,095 g for 3 minutes at room temperature
4. Resuspend pellet in 1 milliliter pasteurized spring water for second centrifugation
5. Transfer 500 microliters of conditioned medium per culture to individual wells of a glass spot plate
6. Transfer one Stentor cell into each well containing medium
7. Feed each Stentor culture with five microliters of prepared Chlamydomonas every 48 hours
8. Maintain cultures in a shaded area
9. Count new Stentor cells before each feeding
10. Adjust volume of delivered Chlamydomonas based on cell count
11. Gently pipette culture medium a few times to detach Stentor from meniscus of each well
12. Use one milliliter pipette to carefully aspirate media from wells without removing cells
13. Add 500 microliters of fresh conditioned media to each well
14. Add 20 milliliters of pasteurized spring water to autoclaved sterilized wide mouth glass jar
15. Carefully detach Stentor cells from bottom of each well
16. Collect all Stentor cells with one milliliter pipette
17. Gently transfer collected cells to glass jar
18. Add fresh pasteurized spring water to jar every 48 hours to maintain Stentor density at 20 cells/mL
19. Feed Stentor cells with 200-1000 microliters of prepared Chlamydomonas
20. Transfer entire jar contents to two-cup glass container when culture volume reaches 90% capacity
21. Feed transferred culture with 2 milliliters prepared Chlamydomonas per 100 milliliters of culture
22. Add pasteurized spring water every 4-5 days to maintain Stentor density at 20 cells/mL
23. Inspect cultures weekly
24. Inspect cultures under 5X dissecting microscope for rotifers, fungus, and other growth
25. Remove contaminating microorganisms and abnormally shaped/colorless Stentor cells using one milliliter pipette
26. Assess if glass container is approximately 90% full to initiate splitting
27. Add 25 milliliters of pasteurized spring water to culture
28. Detach Stentor from glass using 50 milliliter pipette
29. Transfer approximately 50% of culture to new two-cup glass container
30. Use needle puller to make needles from capillary tubes
31. Collect one healthy Stentor with trumpet shape, blue-green color, and no large vacuoles in a two microliter droplet
32. Place droplet on slide
33. Add two microliters of 4% methyl cellulose to slow Stentor motion
34. Place droplet under dissecting microscope
35. Hold glass needle parallel to cutting surface to prevent breakage
36. Gently press contracted Stentor with side of needle
37. Split anterior end from posterior end of cell
38. Confirm both fragments have at least one macronuclear node
39. Move fragments into individual wells of glass spot plate
40. Transfer 30-60 Stentor cells in 1 ml culture medium to microcentrifuge tube
41. Collect all cells from tube using 200μl pipette in single 125μl draw
42. Dispense cells into tube containing 500μl of 25% sucrose solution
43. Start stopwatch for sucrose treatment timing
44. Flick spin cells in tube rack for 1 minute
45. Collect all cells in single 200μl draw and hold in pipette tip
46. Hold cells in pipette tip until stopwatch reaches 2 minutes sucrose treatment
47. Eject Stentor cells into microcentrifuge tube with 1 ml pasteurized spring water
48. Perform three flick spin washes
49. Add 100 microliters of pasteurized spring water into one well of a glass spot plate
50. Collect one Stentor cell in four microliters of culture media using a 20 microliter pipette tip
51. Deposit the droplet onto the center of a 22x22 mm coverslip
52. Place four additional droplets around the central droplet
53. Invert coverslip and gently place it over the well containing pasteurized spring water
54. Image regenerating cells under light microscope with appropriate time resolution

Complete step list: Mix NK cell isolation cocktail solution with 6-10 milliliters of EDTA peripheral whole blood by several inversions
2. Homogenize sample on tube rotator for 5 minutes at room temperature
3. Place tube into magnetic separator for 15 minutes under sterile conditions with tube label facing magnet back
4. Transfer supernatant into new 15 milliliter tube
5. Bring final volume to 15 milliliters with complete medium
6. Wash cells by centrifugation
7. Resuspend pellet in 1 milliliter of fresh complete medium
8. Count cells
9. Adjust volume to concentration of at least 2×10⁴ NK cells per 100 microliters in complete medium
10. Gently mix isolated NK cells by pipetting at least five times
11. Aliquot 100 microliters of NK cells into appropriate wells of 96-well V-bottomed plate
12. Switch off light
13. Add anti-CD107a antibody to each well of NK cells
14. Carefully mix aliquot of K562 tumor cells (2×10⁴ cells/100μL) by pipetting at least five times
15. Transfer 100 microliters of tumor cells to each stimulation well
16. Add IL-2 and IL-15 to stimulation wells
17. Mix all wells by pipetting at least five times
18. Incubate plate protected from light for 3 hours at 37°C and 5% CO₂
19. Add freshly prepared protein transport inhibitor solution to each well with careful mixing
20. Return plate to incubator
21. Mix co-cultures carefully
22. Transfer mixed co-cultures to corresponding flow cytometry tubes
23. Add 1 milliliter of wash buffer to each tube
24. Resuspend pellets in 99 microliters of PBS and 1 microliter of fixable dead cell marker per sample
25. Vortex cells
26. Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature in the dark
27. Wash cells in 1 mL wash buffer
28. Resuspend pellets in 84 μL wash buffer plus 16 μL cell surface antibody cocktail
29. Vortex samples
30. Incubate for 20 minutes in the dark at 4°C
31. Wash cells in 1 ml wash buffer
32. Resuspend pellets
33. Resuspend in 100 μl cold fixation solution
34. Mix by vortexing
35. Incubate for 10 minutes at 4°C in dark
36. Wash cells in 1 ml wash buffer
37. Resuspend pellets in 90 μl permeabilization buffer
38. Stain with 10 μl intracellular antibodies and mix by vortexing
39. Incubate for 30 minutes in dark at 4°C
40. Wash cells twice in 1 ml fresh permeabilization buffer
41. Resuspend samples in 400 μl fresh permeabilization buffer
42. Mix by vortexing and place cells on ice for flow cytometry analysis

8. Fill four edges of plate with sterile water to compensate for evaporation

12. Place aspirated ovaries in beaker with sterile saline maintained at 26 degrees Celsius
13. Place one ovary on sterile PTFE cutting board and cut 1.5-2mm thick slices of ovarian cortex parallel to major axis using surgical #22 blade
14. Place slices of ovarian cortex in sterile glass Petri dish with dissecting medium
15. Position dish on warm plate at 38.5°C
16. Transfer one ovarian cortex slice to 60mm glass Petri dish
17. Add 2-3 mL of M199D medium to dish
18. Position dish under dissection microscope
19. Select follicles measuring 0.5-2 mm in diameter
20. Identify healthy non-atretic follicles using morphological parameters (translucent appearance, vascularization, regular granulosa layer)
21. Discard atretic follicles
22. Use surgical blade to remove ovarian tissue surrounding follicle
23. Continue tissue removal until follicle is exposed
24. Use 26 gauge needle to make slit in exposed follicle wall
25. Release follicular content containing COC through slit
26. Identify COC and examine for cumulus integrity
27. Examine COC for zona pellucida integrity and cytoplasm homogeneity
28. Aspirate COC with P20 pipette if integrity criteria are fulfilled
29. Place isolated COC in M199D cilostamide medium
30. Continue isolation procedure for 30 minutes
31. Prepare 16 drops of 20 microliters M199D cilostamide in a 60 millimeter Petri dish
32. Place one healthy COC into each prepared drop
33. Use inverted microscope with camera to measure oocyte diameter (excluding zona pellucida)
34. Make two perpendicular measurements of oocyte diameter under clear visualization
35. Verify mean of two measurements is within 100-110 micrometers range
36. Transfer selected COCs to 35 millimeter dish containing M199H medium
37. Transfer one COC into center of each well of pre-prepared 96-well plate
38. Incubate plate for five days at 38.5°C and 5% CO₂ with maximum humidity
39. Replace 100 microliters of old medium with 100 microliters of fresh long IVCO medium
40. Perform medium replacement under stereo microscope to avoid disturbing COCs

prompt:
Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Collect bulk soil samples using ethanol-sterilized soil core collector at 23-30 cm depth from plant base
2. Transfer collected soil to plastic bag
3. Homogenize soil by gentle shaking of plastic bag
4. Transfer 600-milligram soil aliquot into two-milliliter tube
5. Place two-milliliter tube on dry ice for preservation until DNA extraction
6. Dig up plant using ethanol-sterilized shovel while preserving root mass
7. Gently shake excess soil from roots until approximately 2mm of soil adheres to root surface
8. For large plants, cut representative root subsection using sterile scissors
9. Place minimum 500mg root tissue into 50-milliliter conical vial
10. Add epiphyte removal buffer until roots are covered
11. Immediately place sample on dry ice
12. Thaw root sample on ice
13. Sonicate root samples
14. Transfer roots to chilled 50-milliliter tube using sterile forceps
15. Centrifuge tube containing buffer and rhizosphere fraction
16. Decant supernatant
17. Place rhizosphere fraction in dry ice
18. Add 20 milliliters of 4°C sterile water to root fraction
19. Transfer 250 milligrams of soil and rhizosphere sample into commercial DNA isolation kit collection tubes using sterile spatula
20. Store extracted DNA at -20°C after elution
21. Chill sterilized mortar and pestle with liquid nitrogen
22. Measure 600-700 mg of root tissue
23. Place measured root tissue into mortar
24. Add sufficient liquid nitrogen to cover roots in mortar
25. Grind roots into small pieces
26. Repeat liquid nitrogen addition and grinding process ≥2 times consistently
27. Grind until roots become fine powder
28. Transfer root powder using sterile spatula to pre-weighed 1.5-mL tubes on ice before thawing
29. Prepare sufficient PCR master mix for triplicate amplification of each DNA sample
30. Pour master mix into sterile 25-milliliter multichannel pipette reservoir
31. Distribute 66 microliters of master mix into each well of new 96-well PCR plate
32. Add 6 microliters of 5 nanograms/microliter DNA from normalized DNA plate to master mix plate
33. Add 1.5 microliters of 10 micromolar forward primer with column-specific barcodes to master plate
34. Add 1.5 microliters of 10 micromolar reverse primer with row-specific barcodes to master plate
35. Cover reaction plate with sealing film
36. Centrifuge plate briefly at 3,000 RCF
37. Gently mix plate contents using multichannel pipette
38. Divide mixture into three plates with 25 microliters each
39. Cover all plates with PCR sealing film
40. Amplify DNA in plates using thermocycler
41. Pool three replicate amplification plates into a single 96-well plate
42. Calculate volume for 100 nanograms of each sample and average volume using computer spreadsheet
43. Add calculated average volume of blank PCR product into 1.5-milliliter tube
44. Pool 100 nanograms of each successfully amplified sample into the same 1.5-milliliter tube
45. Measure concentration of pooled product using benchtop fluorometer
46. Elute 600 nanograms of DNA in molecular-grade water to final volume of 100 microliters in 1.5-milliliter tube
47. Prepare 600 microliters of fresh 70% ethanol
48. Shake tube of magnetic beads to resuspend settled beads
49. Add 100 microliters of bead solution to 600-nanogram DNA aliquot
50. Mix solution and beads by pipetting 10 times
51. Incubate mixture for five minutes at room temperature
52. Place tube on magnetic stand for two minutes or until solution clears
53. Keep tube in magnetic stand
54. Aspirate clear supernatant carefully without touching magnetic beads
55. Add 300 microliters of 70% ethanol to tube
56. Incubate beads at room temperature for 30 seconds
57. Aspirate out ethanol and discard
58. Remove tube from magnetic stand
59. Air-dry contents for five minutes
60. Add 30 microliters of molecular-grade water to dried beads
61. Mix sample by pipetting 10 times
62. Incubate at room temperature for two minutes
63. Place tube on magnetic stand for one minute to separate beads from solution
64. Transfer eluate to new tube
65. Measure DNA concentration using benchtop fluorometer
66. Dilute aliquot to 10 nanomolar in 30 microliters (or to sequencing facility specifications)

6. Place tissue on TARE disposable weigh boats
7. Place weighing boat with brain tissue into polystyrene containers with dry ice to prevent thawing
8. Remove weigh boat containing tissue piece from dry ice after dissection and weighing
9. Add five milliliters of ice cold low-salt buffer
10. Add 5 ml of ice-cold low-salt buffer with protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail per gram of tissue
11. Homogenize tissue on ice using 10 strokes of high-clearance pestle A followed by 15 strokes of low-clearance pestle B
12. Transfer homogenate to labeled 2-ml polypropylene tube using nine-inch glass Pasteur pipette
13. Aliquot remaining homogenate into labeled 1.5-ml tubes for storage at -80°C
14. Add 100 microliters of 5M sodium chloride and 100 microliters of 10% sarkosyl to each 0.8-milliliter aliquot
15. Mix aliquots well by inversion
16. Incubate aliquots on ice for 15 minutes
17. Sonicate aliquots using microtip probe: three 5-second pulses at 30% amplitude
18. Add ice-cold sark buffer with protease and phosphatase inhibitors to each sample
19. Adjust samples to final concentration of 10 milligrams per milliliter
20. Transfer 500 microliters of each sample into 500-microliter polycarbonate ultracentrifuge tubes
21. Load tubes into prechilled rotor
22. Ultracentrifuge samples at 180,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C
23. Transfer S1 sarkosyl-soluble supernatants
24. Transfer S1 sarkosyl-soluble supernatants to 1.5-milliliter tubes
25. Store supernatants at -80°C
26. Add 200 microliters of sark buffer to ultracentrifuge tubes containing P1 fractions
27. Dislodge pellets from tube bottoms using pipette tip
28. Transfer resuspended P1 pellets to new 500-microliter ultracentrifuge tubes
29. Pair-balance tubes and centrifuge at 180,000×g for 30 minutes at 4°C
30. Discard S2 supernatant
31. Add 50-75 microliters of urea buffer with protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail to sarkosyl-insoluble pellets
32. Incubate mixture for 30 minutes at room temperature to solubilize P2 pellet
33. Transfer re-suspended P2 pellets to labeled 0.5-milliliter tubes
34. Fully solubilize pellets using brief one-second microtip sonication at 20% amplitude
35. Determine protein concentrations of sarkosyl-soluble and sarkosyl-insoluble fractions using BCA assay method
36. Prepare 40-microgram samples of total homogenate, sark-soluble S1 fraction, and sark-insoluble P2 fraction in 1x Laemmli SDS-PAGE sample buffer with 5 mM TCEP at pH 7
37. Incubate samples at 95 degrees Celsius for 5 minutes
38. Load samples onto precast 10-well 4-12% Bis-Tris SDS-PAGE gels
39. Electrophorese at 80 volts until migration of first centimeter, then at 120 volts until tracking dye reaches gel bottom (approximately 1 hour)
40. Submerge precast gel cassettes in distilled water and split open using fresh razor blade and gel knife
41. Cut away combs and very bottom of each gel with fresh razor blade
42. Transfer gels to 0.2 micron nitrocellulose membranes using dry transfer method on blotting machine
43. Block membranes in blocking buffer without Tween-20 for 30 minutes
44. Block membranes in blocking buffer with 0.5% Tween-20 for 30 minutes
45. Rinse membranes in TBS with 0.1% Tween-20 for five minutes to remove excess blocking buffer
46. Prepare 1:1,000 dilutions of primary antibodies in blocking buffer with 0.5% Tween-20
47. Incubate membranes in primary antibody solution overnight at 4°C with circular agitation
48. Rinse membranes three times in TBS with 0.1% Tween-20 (15 minutes per rinse)
49. Probe membranes with 1:20,000 dilution of fluorescently-labeled near-infrared secondary antibody in blocking buffer with 0.5% Tween-20 for 60 minutes at room temperature in darkness on shaker
50. Rinse membrane three times in TBS with 0.1% Tween-20 (10 minutes per rinse) and twice in TBS (5 minutes per rinse)

64. Scrape excess solution from spatula into tube

68. Incubate samples on bench protected from light for 2-4 days

8. Prevent introduction of air bubbles during tubing placement
9. Tighten cap while ensuring seal is properly seated

13. Open outlet port and clear buffer line

19. Separate liver from diaphragm
20. Make small incision in diaphragm using curved blunt scissors
21. Continue diaphragm incision along entire length of rib cage to expose pleural cavity

23. Cut through rib cage up to collarbone
24. Make cut on contralateral side

27. Clamp tip of sternum with hemostat
28. Place hemostat over head

35. Maintain 80 mmHg pressure throughout buffer infusion period
36. Start timer

43. Begin dissection of fixed rat

45. Make midline incision along integument from neck to nose
46. Expose skull

48. Expose base of skull
49. Insert sharp end of iris scissors into foramen magnum on one side
50. Slide scissors along inner surface of skull
51. Make cut extending to distal edge of posterior skull surface
52. Make identical cut on contralateral side
53. Use rongeurs to clear skull around cerebellum
54. Slide scissors tip along inner skull surface from dorsal distal posterior corner to distal frontal ledge
55. Lift blade tip during cutting to avoid brain damage
56. Repeat cutting procedure on opposite side
57. Peel dorsal surface of skull away from brain using rongeurs
58. Trim sides of skull using rongeurs
59. Sever olfactory bulbs and ventral nervous connections using spatula

27. Examine COC for zona pellucida integrity and cytoplasm homogeneity

30. Continue isolation procedure for 30 minutes

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Collect bulk soil samples using ethanol-sterilized soil core collector at 23-30 cm depth from plant base
2. Transfer collected soil to plastic bag
3. Homogenize soil by gentle shaking of plastic bag
4. Transfer 600-milligram soil aliquot into two-milliliter tube
5. Place two-milliliter tube on dry ice for preservation until DNA extraction
6. Dig up plant using ethanol-sterilized shovel while preserving root mass
7. Gently shake excess soil from roots until approximately 2mm of soil adheres to root surface
8. For large plants, cut representative root subsection using sterile scissors
9. Place minimum 500mg root tissue into 50-milliliter conical vial
10. Add epiphyte removal buffer until roots are covered
11. Immediately place sample on dry ice
12. Thaw root sample on ice
13. Sonicate root samples
14. Transfer roots to chilled 50-milliliter tube using sterile forceps
15. Centrifuge tube containing buffer and rhizosphere fraction
16. Decant supernatant
17. Place rhizosphere fraction in dry ice
18. Add 20 milliliters of 4°C sterile water to root fraction
19. Transfer 250 milligrams of soil and rhizosphere sample into commercial DNA isolation kit collection tubes using sterile spatula
20. Store extracted DNA at -20°C after elution
21. Chill sterilized mortar and pestle with liquid nitrogen
22. Measure 600-700 mg of root tissue
23. Place measured root tissue into mortar
24. Add sufficient liquid nitrogen to cover roots in mortar
25. Grind roots into small pieces
26. Repeat liquid nitrogen addition and grinding process ≥2 times consistently
27. Grind until roots become fine powder
28. Transfer root powder using sterile spatula to pre-weighed 1.5-mL tubes on ice before thawing
29. Prepare sufficient PCR master mix for triplicate amplification of each DNA sample
30. Pour master mix into sterile 25-milliliter multichannel pipette reservoir
31. Distribute 66 microliters of master mix into each well of new 96-well PCR plate
32. Add 6 microliters of 5 nanograms/microliter DNA from normalized DNA plate to master mix plate
33. Add 1.5 microliters of 10 micromolar forward primer with column-specific barcodes to master plate
34. Add 1.5 microliters of 10 micromolar reverse primer with row-specific barcodes to master plate
35. Cover reaction plate with sealing film
36. Centrifuge plate briefly at 3,000 RCF
37. Gently mix plate contents using multichannel pipette
38. Divide mixture into three plates with 25 microliters each
39. Cover all plates with PCR sealing film
40. Amplify DNA in plates using thermocycler
41. Pool three replicate amplification plates into a single 96-well plate
42. Calculate volume for 100 nanograms of each sample and average volume using computer spreadsheet
43. Add calculated average volume of blank PCR product into 1.5-milliliter tube
44. Pool 100 nanograms of each successfully amplified sample into the same 1.5-milliliter tube
45. Measure concentration of pooled product using benchtop fluorometer
46. Elute 600 nanograms of DNA in molecular-grade water to final volume of 100 microliters in 1.5-milliliter tube
47. Prepare 600 microliters of fresh 70% ethanol
48. Shake tube of magnetic beads to resuspend settled beads
49. Add 100 microliters of bead solution to 600-nanogram DNA aliquot
50. Mix solution and beads by pipetting 10 times
51. Incubate mixture for five minutes at room temperature
52. Place tube on magnetic stand for two minutes or until solution clears
53. Keep tube in magnetic stand
54. Aspirate clear supernatant carefully without touching magnetic beads
55. Add 300 microliters of 70% ethanol to tube
56. Incubate beads at room temperature for 30 seconds
57. Aspirate out ethanol and discard
58. Remove tube from magnetic stand
59. Air-dry contents for five minutes
60. Add 30 microliters of molecular-grade water to dried beads
61. Mix sample by pipetting 10 times
62. Incubate at room temperature for two minutes
63. Place tube on magnetic stand for one minute to separate beads from solution
64. Transfer eluate to new tube
65. Measure DNA concentration using benchtop fluorometer
66. Dilute aliquot to 10 nanomolar in 30 microliters (or to sequencing facility specifications)

4. Position mouse on its back slightly tilted onto its right side
5. Cut away fur along mouse's left side between front and back legs using dissecting scissors
6. Grab peritoneum with forceps and carefully make an incision without damaging spleen
7. Remove spleen with forceps and place into sterile 50 milliliter tube containing approximately 10 milliliters of culture media on ice
8. Transfer spleen with 2 milliliters of culture medium to sterile Petri dish
9. Homogenize spleen by grinding between frosted portions of two sterile slides
10. Pipette 2 milliliters of culture medium containing splenocytes through 40 micron nylon cell strainer into 50 milliliter tube
11. Add 8 milliliters of cold culture medium to 50 milliliter tube containing splenocytes
12. Determine cell concentration per milliliter using hemocytometer
13. Add 1 × 10⁶ cells per well to six-well culture plates
14. Add 3 ml of culture medium or challenge medium to wells
15. Incubate plates at 37°C and 5% CO₂ for 3 hours
16. Scrape cells from well bottom using P1000 micropipette with 1,000 microliter tip
17. Transfer cell-containing medium to 15 milliliter tube using same pipette tip
18. Pellet cells via centrifugation at 167 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature
19. Remove supernatant from pelleted cells
20. Wash cell pellet with 5 milliliters of PBS
21. Repellet cells via centrifugation at 167 × g for 5 minutes
22. Remove supernatant after second pelleting
23. Add 600 microliters of lysis buffer to cell pellet
24. Isolate RNA from splenocytes using RNA extraction kit

1. Fix pancreas sample in freshly prepared 4% paraformaldehyde

4. Place bucket on magnetic stir plate
5. Position flask flat in bucket
6. Add magnetic stir bar to flask
7. Pour 147.8 milliliters of ice-cold distilled deionized water into flask
8. Add 20 milliliters of 0.1 molar PBS
9. Add 20 milliliters of ice-cold 40% acrylamide solution
10. Add 12.2 milliliters of 16% paraformaldehyde solution
11. Add 250 milligrams of VA-044 initiator
12. Mix entire hydrogel solution for at least 10 minutes
13. Place 15 milliliter conical tube in ice next to flask containing hydrogel solution
14. Pipette 14 milliliters of monomer solution into conical tube
15. Add one piece of fixed and sectioned tissue sample to tube
16. Cap conical tube
17. Incubate sample in monomer solution for 3 days at 4°C protected from light
18. Place sample on ice
19. Connect tubing to nitrogen tank through stopcock
20. Pierce cap of conical tube containing sample with 18 gauge hypodermic needle
21. Insert needle into tube until submerged under surface of liquid monomer solution
22. Puncture opposite side of cap with 18-gauge hypodermic needle
23. Ensure needle remains unsubmerged to act as vent
24. Connect nitrogen tank tubing to submerged hypodermic needle beneath hydrogel
25. Slowly turn on nitrogen until steady bubbling through liquid
26. Remove both needles after deoxygenation
27. Cover cap with paraffin film to prevent gas exchange
28. Incubate sample at 37°C for three hours to polymerize hydrogel
29. Pour away remaining hydrogel
30. Wash sample in 3-5 exchanges of 0.01 M PBS for 15 minutes per wash
31. Transfer sample to 50 ml conical tube containing 40 ml clearing buffer
32. Incubate sample in clearing buffer at 37°C with buffer replacement every other day
33. Verify clearing by holding sample to light and confirming light transmission with tan coloring in exocrine regions
34. Exchange clearing buffer with 40 milliliters of 0.01 molar PBS
35. Place samples on shaker at 60 RPM for one day at room temperature
36. Perform 4-5 buffer changes
37. Continue final wash overnight
38. Prepare PACT staining buffer in 2 milliliter flat bottom tube
39. Add 2% normal serum to 1 milliliter base PACT buffer
40. Add approximately five times standard amount of primary antibody to staining buffer
41. Remove sample from wash buffer using spatula
42. Dab excess buffer onto paper towel
43. Place sample into tube containing primary antibody solution
44. Incubate sample in solution for 2-4 days at room temperature on shaker at 60 RPM
45. Remove primary antibody solution
46. Add 0.01 molar PBS
47. Wash samples on shaker at 60 RPM
48. Replace PBS buffer 4-5 times during washing
49. Leave final wash on shaker overnight
50. Prepare secondary antibody at 1:200 dilution in PACT staining buffer with 2% serum
51. Remove sample from wash buffer using a spatula
52. Dab excess buffer off sample onto paper towel
53. Place sample in tube containing secondary antibody solution
54. Incubate sample at room temperature on shaker at 60 RPM for two days with light protection
55. Remove antibody solution following incubation
56. Replace solution with 0.01 molar PBS
57. Wash samples thoroughly on shaker at 60 RPM with 4-5 buffer changes, leaving final wash overnight
58. Weigh 11 grams of non-ionic density gradient medium
59. Transfer weighed medium to 50 milliliter conical tube
60. Add 5 milliliters of 0.02 molar phosphate buffer to tube
61. Use spatula to release air from powdered medium
62. Adjust volume to 10 milliliters using additional 0.02 molar phosphate buffer
63. Mix solution with spatula
64. Scrape excess solution from spatula into tube
65. Incubate buffer at 37 degrees Celsius until fully dissolved
66. Periodically invert and gently mix solution during incubation
67. Transfer samples into refractive index match solution buffer
68. Incubate samples on bench protected from light for 2-4 days
69. Place refractive index match solution into eight-well coverslip bottom chamber slide
70. Add sample to well
71. Cap slide

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Prepare yeast extract with supplements without adenine (YES), Pombe Glutamate Medium (PMG), and PMG without adenine
2. Mix media components according to specified table
3. Add G418 to media after autoclaving if necessary
4. Stir media for 5-10 minutes
5. Aliquot media into 90 milliliter Petri dishes
6. Store plates at 4 degrees Celsius
7. Use cloned rpt4 positive with 5' and 3' UTRs and silent mutation
8. Perform error-prone PCR with primers p5 and p6 and error-prone polymerase in 50 microliter total volume
9. Inoculate 10 milliliters of YES medium with yeast
10. Incubate culture for >16 hours to saturation
11. Dilute cells to OD600 0.2 using 200 milliliters of YES medium
12. Incubate culture at 30°C with shaking for 5-6 hours to OD600 0.6-0.8
13. Calculate volume of cells equivalent to OD600 of 30
14. Dispense cells into four 50ml conical tubes
15. Chill tubes on ice for 10 minutes
16. Harvest cells by centrifugation at 1050 G, 4°C for 3 minutes
17. Place microfuge tubes with cassette DNA and 10 electro cuvettes on ice
18. Discard supernatant while keeping tubes on ice
19. Add 15ml of 1.2M sorbitol
20. Gently shake tubes to resuspend cells
21. Centrifuge at 1050 G, 4°C for 3 minutes
22. Discard supernatant and perform second sorbitol wash
23. Discard supernatant after second centrifugation
24. Resuspend cells and transfer to one 15ml conical tube
25. Add 1.2 molar sorbitol up to 2.4 milliliters
26. Keep tube of cells on ice
27. Add 200 microliters of sorbitol-suspended cells to tube containing fusion PCR construct
28. Mix sample well
29. Transfer sample to electro cuvette
30. Add 600 microliters of 1.2-molar sorbitol to each electroporation cuvette
31. Spread transformed cells onto four YES plates
32. Incubate plates at 30 degrees Celsius for 24 hours
33. Perform replica plating on YES plates containing G418
34. Incubate replica plates for three additional days
35. Perform replica plating from YES plus G418 plates to YES without adenine plates
36. Perform replica plating from YES plus G418 plates to PMG without adenine plates
37. Incubate replica plates at 30°C for 1-2 days until colonies on YES without adenine plates show white coloration
38. Compare growth on YES without adenine and PMG without adenine plates
39. Select colonies showing pink or white coloration on YES without adenine plates with concurrent growth on PMG without adenine plates
40. Exclude colonies without growth on PMG without adenine plates (false positives)
41. Pick each colony and add to 10 microliters of SPZ solution containing 2.5 mg/ml zymolyase 100T
42. Incubate colonies at 37°C for at least 30 minutes
43. Use 1 microliter of incubated solution as template for colony PCR
44. Mark colonies with XhoI-cut PCR products and patch them to YES plus G418 plates
45. Isolate genomic DNA (gDNA) from fission yeast cells
46. Sequence PCR products
47. Compare obtained sequence with wild-type sequence
48. Identify mutations through sequence comparison
49. Re-introduce identified mutations into wild-type cells
50. Confirm phenotype using spotting assay in newly-made mutant cells

1. Calibrate probe sonicator fitted with vial block sonitrobe
2. Measure 2 mg of chosen nanopowder into each of three clean 10 or 20 mL glass vials (numbered 1-3) using clean metal spatula

9. Firmly close microcentrifuge tubes
10. Swirl closed tubes to dislodge nanopowder from inner walls
11. Place samples in sonitrobe
12. Sonicate samples at 1.1 watts
13. Sonicate samples at 1.1 watts with pulse setting (1 second on, 1 second off) for 2 minutes
14. Remove sample one from sonication block
15. Transfer 1 milliliter from top of dispersion to clean microcentrifuge tube
16. Add deionized water to attain sample concentration of 0.02 mg/mL
17. Immediately begin sample characterization
18. Sonicate remaining samples for four minutes
19. Maintain same amplitude and pulse settings during sonication
20. Dilute sample two to 0.02 mg/mL with deionized water
21. Begin characterization of sample two
22. Sonicate sample three for four minutes
23. Maintain same amplitude and pulse settings during sonication
24. Dilute sample three to 0.02 mg/mL
25. Begin characterization of sample three
26. Calibrate ultrasonic bath with respect to bath sensor
27. Place 2 milligrams of nanopowder in each of four clean glass vials using clean spatula
28. Number vials four through seven
29. Pipette 1 milliliter of deionized water along vial walls and mix into thick paste
30. Add deionized water to achieve 0.2 milligrams per milliliter concentration in each vial
31. Cap vials and swirl to dislodge nanopowder adhering to inner surfaces
32. Place vials in center of calibrated ultrasonic bath
33. Ensure water level is halfway up the vials
34. Sonicate sample at 80 watts for 15 minutes at room temperature
35. Transfer aliquot of sample four to clean vial
36. Dilute aliquot with deionized water to 0.02 milligrams per milliliter
37. Begin characterization of diluted sample
38. Replace ultrasonic bath water with fresh room temperature water
39. Open dynamic light scattering instrument software
40. Create size measurement file
41. Configure parameters: equilibration time, temperature, cuvette type, experiment mode
42. Save size measurement file
43. Run DLS verification measurement using standard 100nm latex beads
44. Confirm instrument performance meets standards
45. Slowly pipette 1 mL of dilute nanopowder dispersion into clean low-volume disposable cuvette while avoiding air bubbles
46. Insert cuvette into instrument
47. Start data collection
48. Take at least five measurements per sample
49. Select all measurements
50. Calculate average for each sample
51. Export measurement data to spreadsheet program for analysis
52. Open UV-Vis instrument software and initialize new measurement
53. Pipette 2-3 milliliters of dilute nanopowder dispersion into clean standard quartz cuvette
54. Set instrument wavelength range to 700 nanometers to 200 nanometers
55. Acquire solvent blank spectrum for background subtraction
56. Acquire at least three sample spectra
57. Export spectral data for further analysis
58. Place drop of dilute nanopowder dispersion on 300 mesh holey carbon film
59. Allow sample to air-dry under ambient conditions while protected from airborne contamination
60. Wash grid with ultra pure water to remove effects from uneven drying
61. Acquire TEM images and export them for further analysis

prompt:
Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Place anesthetized mouse in supine position on sterile-draped surgery table
2. Apply ocular lubricant to protect eyes from drying
3. Shave abdominal hair for operation and leg hair for postoperative perfusion measurements using pen trimmer
4. Clear shaved hair off surgical field
5. Fixate upper and lower extremities with rubber bands and tacks
6. Check anesthesia depth via toe pinch reflex and titrate anesthesia as necessary
7. Perform respiratory pattern evaluation every 3-5 minutes to calibrate anesthesia level
8. Perform midline laparotomy from lower sternal margin to pubis symphysis
9. Dissect pubis fat pad to widen operative field
10. Open celiotomy to access peritoneal contents
11. Cover bowels with saline-soaked non-woven sponge
12. Dissect perivascular fascia and adipose tissue from 1 cm proximal to aortic bifurcation to left iliac bifurcation using straight Dumont forceps and double-ended sharp cotton swabs
13. Pass tip of angled forceps under left common iliac vascular bundle
14. Gently spread forceps multiple times to mobilize vessels from retroperitoneal musculature
15. Place two 4-0 silk sutures around isolated left common iliac arteriovenous bundle as ligatures
16. Create single knot with each 4-0 silk tie
17. Apply knots sequentially (proximally then distally)
18. Rotate left iliac arteriovenous bundle clockwise using 4-0 silk suture strings as handles
19. Fine-tune position to temporarily locate vein anterior to artery
20. Make 1mm longitudinal venotomy using straight Vannas spring scissors
21. Flush residual blood from venous lumen with 0.9% saline
22. Place 10-0 nylon suture through posterior wall of vein
23. Grab suture ends and apply gentle tension to separate anterior and posterior vessel walls
24. Make elliptical incision (1.0 × 0.3 mm) using curved Vannas spring scissors
25. Remove adherent walls of iliac artery and vein
26. Flush exposed arterial lumen with 0.9% saline and heparinized saline
27. Repair initial anterior wall venotomy with 2-3 10-0 nylon sutures in interrupted fashion
28. Restore vascular bundle to original anatomic orientation
29. Place saline-soaked absorbable gelatin sponge adjacent to repaired venotomy
30. Loosen 4-0 single knot cross clamp ligatures sequentially from distal to proximal
31. Monitor venotomy site for excessive bleeding
32. Gently rub vascular bundle with double-ended hard sharp-pointed cotton swabs
33. Visualize pulsatile bright red oxygenated blood entering iliac vein and mixing with dark venous blood to confirm fistula success
34. Inject heparinized saline into inferior vena cava for systemic anticoagulation
35. Reinspect surgical site for hemostasis after heparinized saline injection
36. Close midline fascia with absorbable 5-0 PGA sutures in running fashion if no bleeding concerns
37. Close skin incision with absorbable 5-0 PGA sutures in running fashion

35. Collect retained trichomes from each microsieve separately
36. Label each collected trichome size fraction
37. Make tiny holes in cap of tube using sterile needle

39. Transfer powder-like trichomes into labeled pre-chilled 1.5 milliliter tube using pre-chilled spatula
40. Immediately store tubes at -80°C

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Transfer eggs laid by adult moths to two liter boxes
2. Add wax moth substrate to boxes containing eggs
3. Incubate boxes at 30 degrees Celsius in the dark
4. Transfer 25 grams of larva-containing substrate to fresh wax moth substrate after 1-2 weeks when larvae become visible
5. Synchronize larvae by size into groups of 30-40 larvae after two weeks
6. Transfer synchronized larvae groups to new two liter containers with wax moth substrate
7. Select larvae for experiment by weight (180-200mg) after two weeks, choosing only pale, fast-moving specimens
8. Load insulin syringe with blunt-ended needle containing 1 × 10⁷ bacteria per 10 microliters of DPBS per larva
9. Load syringe into microsyringe pump
10. Wait for larva to open mouth parts
11. Insert syringe carefully between larval mandibles
12. Deliver bacterial suspension
13. Incubate fed larvae in dark at 37°C for 1-24 hours
14. Clean safety hood with ethanol
15. Spray reagent to prevent RNase contamination
16. Snap-freeze living larva in liquid nitrogen
17. Homogenize individual frozen larva using mortar and pestle with small volume of liquid nitrogen
18. Transfer powdered homogenate to disposable weigh boat
19. Wait for liquid nitrogen to evaporate
20. Mix powdered homogenates with 1 ml TRIzol in 2 ml tube
21. Incubate mixture at room temperature for 1 hour
22. Pellet homogenate by centrifugation
23. Transfer supernatant to new tube
24. Mix supernatant with 200 μl BCP (1-Bromo-3-chloropropane)
25. Vortex mixture and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature
26. Incubate mixture on ice for 10 minutes
27. Centrifuge BCP-added reaction mixture
28. Transfer upper transparent aqueous layer to new 2 ml tube
29. Add 500 microliters isopropanol to precipitate RNA
30. Mix by inverting tube for 5 minutes
31. Collect precipitated RNA via centrifugation
32. Wash RNA pellet with 500 microliters of 75% ethanol
33. Air-dry RNA pellet for 5-10 minutes at room temperature
34. Add 100 microliters of ribonuclease inhibitor in nuclease-free water to dried RNA pellet
35. Vortex tube until RNA pellet is completely dissolved
36. Measure RNA quality and quantity by spectrophotometry (260/280≈2, 260/230=2-2.2)
37. Prepare 5 micrograms isolated RNA for DNase digestion and gene expression analysis

30. Maintain cover slips with cell-covered side facing up during transfer

Complete step list: Thaw bottle of basement membrane matrix on ice or at 4°C overnight
2. Transfer resected tissue to 10-centimeter sterile Petri dish
3. Examine tissue macroscopically; document morphological characteristics (fatty/vascularized/necrotic), record size/shape, and photograph with ruler
4. Mince tissue into small pieces using sterile number 10 scalpel
5. Transfer minced tissue to 50-milliliter conical tube
6. Add 10 milliliters of 2 mg/mL collagenase IV solution
7. Seal the tube
8. Place sealed tube on orbital shaker at 37°C, 140 RPM, 30° angle for 30-90 minutes
9. Place aliquot of complete medium in bead/water bath at 37°C to pre-warm
10. Resuspend tissue every 15 minutes by vigorous mixing using 5-mL sterile pre-coated serological pipette
11. Monitor dissociation under microscope at ≥5X magnification
12. Centrifuge sample at 400 G for five minutes
13. Aspirate supernatant
14. Add 10 milliliters of AdDF+++
15. Centrifuge sample and carefully aspirate supernatant
16. Add two milliliters of red blood cell lysis buffer (if tissue pellet is partially red)
17. Incubate for five minutes at room temperature (if tissue pellet is partially red)
18. Add 10 milliliters of AdDF+++ to tube
19. Centrifuge at 400 G for five minutes
20. Discard supernatant
21. Resuspend pellet in 50 to 300 microliters
22. Discard supernatant
23. Resuspend pellet in 50-300 microliters of undiluted cold basement membrane matrix
24. Mix suspension by pipetting carefully to avoid bubble formation
25. Plate 300 microliters of basement membrane matrix dome containing organoids per well in pre-warmed six-well tissue culture plate
26. Leave plate undisturbed in hood for 5 minutes
27. Incubate plate at 37°C for 20-30 minutes for matrix solidification
28. Add 3 ml of pre-warmed complete medium dropwise to each well
29. Incubate plate at 37°C and 5% CO₂
30. Capture organoid images using 5X objective on inverted bright-field microscope
31. Lift basement membrane matrix dome into well medium using cell scraper or 1-ml pipette tip
32. Transfer floating organoid dome with medium to 15-ml or 50-ml conical tube using pre-coated pipette tip
33. Add DPBS to increase volume to at least 5 milliliters
34. Centrifuge tubes at 400 G for 5 minutes to form basement membrane matrix-organoid layer
35. Aspirate supernatant
36. Add 5-20 ml DPBS (volume dependent on number of wells pooled)
37. Mix organoid-basement membrane matrix pellet in DPBS using pre-coated sterile disposable pipette
38. Centrifuge and discard supernatant
39. Add cell dissociation reagent using coated pipette tip at three times basement membrane matrix volume
40. Resuspend organoids in dissociation reagent
41. Place tube on orbital shaker at 37°C and 140 RPM in angled position for 8-15 minutes
42. Monitor dissociation progress under microscope every five minutes to ensure organoid breakdown
43. Add AdDF+++ at volume equal to or greater than cell dissociation reagent
44. Pipette to mix organoids
45. Centrifuge at 400 G for five minutes to obtain organoid pellet
46. Discard supernatant
47. Resuspend pellet in one milliliter of AdDF+++
48. Adjust volume to 10 milliliters with AdDF+++
49. Centrifuge tube for wash step
50. Discard supernatant after wash step
51. Add required amount of basement membrane matrix to digested organoids based on split ratio
52. Mix by gently pipetting up and down to avoid bubbles
53. Immediately place mixture on ice
54. Plate 300-microliter domes of organoid-matrix suspension in pre-warmed six-well plate
55. Leave plate undisturbed in hood for 5 minutes
56. Incubate plate at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for 20-30 minutes for dome solidification
57. Add 3 mL pre-warmed complete medium to each well
58. Place plate back in incubator

1. Crush dry ice block into fine flakes using hammer and hard flat object in 5L plastic container

4. Add 10g frozen cannabis sativa inflorescences onto dry ice layer and cover with additional 200cc finely crushed dry ice

10. Set aside beaker every 2-3 minutes to allow sifting of accumulated dry ice and plant material on flour sieve
11. Sift flour sieve horizontally to pass plant material into liquid nitrogen in stainless steel container below
12. Add liquid nitrogen to stainless steel container when level runs low
13. Add crushed dry ice to one liter glass beaker when level runs low
14. Refill glass beaker containing used plant material with 10 grams of fresh plant material
15. Repeat sifting process until sufficient enriched trichomes accumulate in container
16. Verify presence of white powder-like substance at bottom of stainless steel container submerged in liquid nitrogen
17. Add small amount of liquid nitrogen
18. Add liquid nitrogen to clean small round-bottom stainless steel container
19. Fold 40x40 cm microsieve (150 μm mesh) twice to obtain 20x20 cm fold
20. Open folded microsieve into cone-like shape
21. Secure mesh cone to container edge with clothespins, positioning cone upright with pointed end submerged in liquid nitrogen
22. Pour liquid nitrogen containing white powder-like substance into microsieve cone
23. Gather and transfer residual plant material from first container into mesh cone using wide brush
24. Detach clothespin from container lid
25. Open microsieve cone
26. Locate trichomes in middle of opened microsieve
27. Hold all four corners of microsieve together
28. Submerge middle part containing trichomes in liquid nitrogen
29. Gently dip and shake microsieve in liquid nitrogen for one minute
30. Puncture cap of 50 milliliter test tube with sterile needle to create vent holes
31. Transfer non-sifted plant debris, dry ice, and larger trichomes from microsieve center into 50 milliliter test tube
32. Store filled test tube at -80 degrees Celsius
33. Transfer sifted trichomes submerged in liquid nitrogen sequentially through 105μm, 80μm, and 65μm microsieves
34. Transfer sample through 50μm microsieve
35. Collect retained trichomes from each microsieve separately
36. Label each collected trichome size fraction
37. Make tiny holes in cap of tube using sterile needle
38. Transfer trichomes (submerged in liquid nitrogen and wrapped in 50 micrometer microsieve) to clean plate using pre-chilled spoon
39. Transfer powder-like trichomes into labeled pre-chilled 1.5 milliliter tube using pre-chilled spatula
40. Immediately store tubes at -80°C
41. Carefully perform T bag-like infusion motion of 150 to 50 micro microsieved isolation

1. Place eight-day-old specific pathogen-free embryonated chicken eggs in rotating egg tray with stamped ends facing upward
2. Set rotating tray inside egg incubator set to 36°C with 50% humidity
3. Incubate eggs for 48 hours
4. Place incubated eggs in egg rack with stamped ends up
5. Transfer egg rack to laminar flow hood
6. Turn off room and hood lights
7. Hold stamped end of egg lightly to egg candler to expose vasculature of chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) and air sack
8. Make a mark between two major blood vessels with a pencil
9. Make a hole at egg tip above air sack at stamped end using sterile push pin (3mm deep)
10. Make a second hole at pencil mark using sterile push pin (3mm deep)
11. Squeeze air from safety bulb
12. Press safety bulb firmly against hole above air sack
13. Slowly release bulb to apply suction at pencil mark hole
14. Confirm air sack displacement to pencil mark using candler
15. Make both holes deeper if air sack displacement unsuccessful
16. Deepen both holes slightly
17. Reapply suction using safety bulb
18. Hold egg with one hand and position rotary tool with 1.5-1.6 inch cutoff wheel attachment
19. Make two transverse cuts (2 cm length, 1 cm apart) through shell without touching CAM
20. Make longitudinal cuts at ends of transverse cuts by lightly touching cutoff wheel to shell
21. Slide sterile forceps under and parallel to shell piece
22. Grab shell piece with forceps and cleanly remove it
23. Place basement membrane protein mixture (e.g., matrigel) on ice to prevent polymerization
24. Use 4-5 ml of 2 mM EDTA solution per flask to detach tumor cells
25. Place flask in tissue culture incubator for 5 minutes
26. Resuspend detached cells in medium
27. Count cell number
28. Transfer volume required for 500,000-2 million cells to new tube
29. Centrifuge tube at 500 × g for 5 minutes
30. Discard supernatant
31. Resuspend cell pellet in 40 μl PBS containing calcium
32. Peel tape off the egg
33. Drop sterile 1 mm silicone ring from cryogenic vial through opening onto CAM
34. Pipette 60 microliter solution of cells, PBS plus plus, and basement membrane mixture into center of silicone ring
35. Retape the egg window
36. Carefully move egg tray back to incubator
37. Allow tumors to grow for 5-7 days
38. Place underpad and biohazard bag in hood
39. Prepare 35 mm × 10 mm plates containing 1 ml PBS plus plus and paraformaldehyde containers
40. Insert pointed end of sterile dissection scissors into egg at hole near stamped end and cut around length of entire egg
41. Extract tumor from CAM using dissection scissors and forceps
42. Place tumor in 35 mm × 10 mm plate
43. Measure and weigh tumor
44. Fix tumor in paraformaldehyde for paraffin embedding
45. Mince harvested tumor in plate using dissection scissors
46. Transfer minced tumor to 15 mL centrifuge tube
47. Remove PBS plus plus from tube by pipetting
48. Add 2 mL of 1 mg/mL collagenase solution in PBS plus plus
49. Mix solution by inverting tube several times
50. Incubate tube at 37°C for 30 minutes to several hours
51. Add 5 mL medium to tube and mix by pipetting 20-40 times
52. Transfer supernatant to fresh tube after sedimentation
53. Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes and discard supernatant

11. Place sterilized silicone ring on CAM surface along small capillaries while avoiding major blood vessels
12. Apply 30 microliters of hypericin solution to silicone ring under sterile conditions
13. Keep embryos in incubator at 37 degrees Celsius in 80-90% humidity
14. Illuminate CAM with violet excitation light
15. Record hypericin and CAM tissue fluorescence with digital camera at timed intervals
16. Record CAM in white light before hypericin administration (if required)
17. Record CAM in white light before tissue fixation (if required)
18. Place CAM under optical fiber to cover entire silicone ring area with laser beam
19. Perform in vivo irradiation with 405nm laser at 285 mW/cm² fluence rate
20. Record CAM images using white light and/or fluorescent light before and after treatment
21. Fix CAM tissue in cultivation plate with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS
22. Remove paraformaldehyde solution
23. Cut out target tissue from CAM within silicone ring
24. Wash excised CAM tissue in water for 10 minutes
25. Dehydrate tissue in 70% ethanol for 3 minutes
26. Stain tissue in eosin solution for 2 minutes
27. Dehydrate tissue in 96% ethanol for 5 minutes
28. Dehydrate tissue in 100% ethanol for 5 minutes
29. Treat tissue with xylene for 10 minutes (first treatment)
30. Treat tissue with xylene for 10 minutes (second treatment)
31. Incubate samples twice in xylene for 10 minutes in a new Petri dish
32. Transfer samples to dissolved paraffin in Petri dishes using spatula or thin brush
33. Place tissue in histological mold after 24 hours
34. Fill histological mold with paraffin embedding medium
35. Allow paraffin to solidify in refrigerator
36. Cut solidified CAM from embedding medium
37. Turn sample in tray by 90 degrees
38. Refill tray with embedding medium
39. Allow embedding medium to solidify
40. Prepare 5-10 micrometer sections using microtome
41. Mount native or 4% paraformaldehyde fixed CAM on glass slide
42. Fill embedding mold halfway with OCT medium
43. Freeze mold in liquid nitrogen or dry ice/ethanol mixture
44. Transfer CAM from glass slide onto frozen OCT medium
45. Place CAM in mold, cover with OCT medium, and freeze
46. Overflow CAM with prewarmed fixation solution (4% paraformaldehyde and 2% glutaraldehyde in PBS)
47. Remove fixation solution after 48 hours
48. Carefully separate CAM from embryo using micro scissors and fine brush
49. Wash separated CAM in PBS
50. Mount washed CAM on glass slide
51. Let mounted CAM slowly dry
52. Photograph slide using digital camera with transilluminator as homogenous white light source

1. Wash neonatal foreskin twice with 5 ml wash media in 5 ml conical tube

4. Rewash foreskin with wash media
5. Place foreskin epidermis side up in six-well plate containing 2 ml Dispase enzyme diluted in wash media
6. Transfer plate to incubator for 4 hours
7. Transfer incubated foreskin to Petri dish
8. Separate epidermis from dermis layer using fine-tip forceps
9. Place epidermis into 15 ml conical tube containing 2 ml of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA
10. Crush floating epidermis using 5 ml serological pipette
11. Incubate sample for 15 minutes at 37°C with periodic vortexing (5 seconds every 5 minutes)
12. Add 2 ml soybean trypsin inhibitor
13. Mix by pipetting to neutralize trypsin
14. Centrifuge cell suspension
15. Resuspend pellet in 12 milliliters of complete KSFM-SCM medium
16. Plate cells in 10 centimeter dish
17. Incubate dish overnight at 37 degrees Celsius and 5% carbon dioxide
18. Remove medium using aspirating pipette
19. Replace medium with 12 milliliters of complete KSFM-SCM
20. Repeat medium replacement procedure on days four and seven
21. Add 2.5 grams of agarose to 50 milliliters of PBS in a 100 milliliter glass bottle
22. Autoclave the bottle on liquid cycle
23. Allow agarose solution to cool to room temperature
24. Place cooled agarose bottle in a one liter beaker filled with 200 milliliters of deionized water
25. Melt agarose mixture in research-grade microwave for up to two minutes
26. Mix agarose every 60 seconds by gently tilting bottle side to side
27. Add 3 milliliters of melted 5% agarose to 12 milliliters of prewarmed KSFM-SCM at 42°C to achieve 1% final concentration
28. Dispense 200 microliters of 1% agarose mix into each well of 96-well plate using multi-channel pipetter
29. Aspirate media from spheroid-forming normal human keratinocytes
30. Wash cells with two milliliters of PBS
31. Aspirate PBS from cells
32. Add two milliliters of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA to washed cells
33. Incubate cells for five minutes at 37 degrees Celsius
34. Add two milliliters of soybean trypsin inhibitor to plate
35. Wash cells from plate into 15 milliliter tube
36. Centrifuge at 250 times G for five minutes
37. Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL PBS
38. Quantify cells using Trypan Blue staining
39. Aliquot 20,000 normal human keratinocytes in 100 μL KSFM-SCM
40. Seed cells in each well of prepared 96-well plate
41. Incubate plate overnight
42. Analyze seeded wells for epidermis sphere formation using inverted phase contrast microscope
43. Add 4 ml of prewarmed KSFM-SCM at 37°C to six-centimeter dish
44. Transfer single spheroid to plate using wide-bore 1 ml pipette tip
45. Incubate plate overnight
46. Analyze seeded spheroid for attaching/propagating cells using inverted phase contrast microscope
47. Remove media from plate
48. Add 2 ml of fresh KSFM-SCM media to plate
49. Quantify cell viability using Trypan Blue and automated cell counter
50. Aliquot 100 microliters containing 100,000 to 4 million keratinocytes into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes
51. Place tubes on ice in dark environment by turning off laminar hood lights
52. Add 2 μL FITC-conjugated anti-integrin alpha six and 2 μL PE-conjugated anti-EGFR to tubes for 1:50 dilution
53. Prepare tube without antibodies for unstained control
54. Incubate tubes on ice in dark for 30 minutes
55. Perform flow cytometry analysis with appropriate lasers
56. Use negative and positive controls to establish gates
57. Sort epidermal stem cell fraction, proliferative progenitor fraction, and committed progenitor fraction
58. Transfer sorted cells from sorting tubes into 15 ml conical tubes containing 10x volume of PBS
59. Centrifuge tubes at 250 × g for 5 minutes
60. Remove supernatant from tubes
61. Resuspend pellet in 4 mL of KSFM-SCM
62. Transfer resuspended cells to 6 cm plate
63. Incubate plate overnight at 37°C in 5% CO₂ incubator with 95% humidity
64. Remove media from plates
65. Add 4 mL of prewarmed KSFM-SCM (37°C) to plates
66. Repeat media change with 4 mL prewarmed KSFM-SCM every 3 days until 70-80% confluency

prompt:
Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Use laryngoscope to expose vocal cords through mouth of 25-30g female Yorkshire pig
2. Spray vocal cords with two puffs of 2% lidocaine topical solution
3. Intubate with 6.5 millimeter tube
4. Use syringe to inflate tube cuff with 3-5 milliliters of air
5. Ensure tracheal tube is in proper position
6. Apply ointment to animal's eyes
7. Protect eyes with cover patch
8. Disinfect neck and abdominal wall with 1% iodine-based scrub solution
9. Make vertical midline anterior neck incision to sternum using number 23 blade
10. Dissect strap muscles
11. Retract muscles laterally using Kelly tissue scissors and Lahey retractor to expose trachea from first ring to thoracic inlet
12. Expose common carotid artery and internal jugular vein for anastomosis
13. Create 1 cm window in second or third tracheal cartilage using number 11 blade
14. Verify endotracheal tube placement through tracheal defect and confirm continuous aeration
15. Design flap on upper abdomen using surgical marking pen
16. Create 4x3 cm elliptical skin incision through anterior sheath using #23 scalpel
17. Position incision on medial side of flap
18. Hold fascia with Allis clamp
19. Elevate flap from rectus abdominis muscle sheath
20. Locate perforators going to skin flap
21. Perform blunt dissection of exposed muscle tissue
22. Follow perforators to superior epigastric vessels
23. Make lateral skin incision in flap using number 23 scalpel
24. Clamp superior epigastric vessels and venae comitantes with haemostat
25. Cut above haemostat using Kelly tissue scissors
26. Ligate vessel below haemostat with three-oh suture to allow haemostat removal
27. Clamp carotid artery with two haemostats placed 1-2 cm apart
28. Cut between haemostats using microscissors
29. Tie superior part of vessel with double suture to prevent leakage
30. Place first two stay sutures 120 degrees apart around vessel circumference using 10-0 simple full thickness interrupted suture
31. Place 2-3 stitches between stay sutures
32. Release vascular clamp
33. Check anastomosis for leakage
34. Create anastomosis between internal jugular vein and venae comitantes
35. Prick skin flap with 18-gauge needle syringe to test viability
36. Observe for blood droplet appearance at puncture site
37. Close tracheal window using 3-0 suture with muscle fascia of superior epigastric artery perforator flap
38. Exteriorize skin panel of flap
39. Suture flap skin panel to cervical midline skin incision
40. Close abdominal skin incision

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Enter nucleotide sequence in empty box
2. In Basic Options box, select minimum free energy and avoid isolated base pairs
3. In Output Options box, select interactive RNA secondary structure plot
4. Click Proceed button
5. Select three different 21 to 24-nucleotide-long sequences within mRNA of interest
6. Prioritize sequences in regions lacking extensive secondary structures and located in 3-prime untranslated regions
7. Select regions with guanidine/cytosine ratio close to 50% and lacking nucleotide tandem repeats
8. Design 2-prime-methoxy modified RNA oligonucleotides bearing biotin moiety at 3-prime end
9. Ensure oligonucleotides are fully complementary to selected target mRNA regions
10. Use online tool to adjust RNA hybrid melting temperature to 60-65°C
11. Optimize linguistic sequence complexity using online tool
12. Select Nucleotide BLAST
13. Insert ASO sequence into query box
14. Select target organism database
15. Keep BLAST parameters as default
16. Initiate BLAST analysis
17. Mix 2 μg reporter gene with 20 μL transfection reagent
18. Add transfection mixture to HEK293 cells (70% confluency in 10-cm dish)
19. Incubate transfected cells at 37°C for 48 hours
20. Remove culture medium using serological pipette
21. Wash cells twice with 10 milliliters of PBS pre-warmed to 37 degrees Celsius
22. Add six milliliters of PBS to dish
23. Place dish on ice
24. Expose cells to UV light at 100 millijoules per square centimeter in UV-crosslinker
25. Scrape off cells and PBS from dish and transfer to 15-milliliter tube
26. Centrifuge cells at 250 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C
27. Remove supernatant using pipette
28. Resuspend cell pellet in 2 ml pre-chilled lysis buffer by pipetting up/down 5-6 times while maintaining tube on ice
29. Transfer lysate to 5 ml tube using pipette while keeping tube on ice
30. Sonicate lysate for 3 rounds (20-second bursts at 10-micron amplitude with 30-second ice-cooling intervals between rounds)
31. Transfer lysate to 2 ml tubes
32. Centrifuge lysate at 15,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C
33. Collect supernatant and transfer to new tube
34. Equilibrate 1 mg oligo(dT)-coupled magnetic beads in 500 μl lysis buffer
35. Remove tube from rotator
36. Place tube on magnetic rack
37. Remove lysis buffer
38. Combine 4 mg HEK293 protein extract with oligo(dT)25-coupled magnetic beads
39. Mix samples vigorously
40. Incubate mixture for 10 minutes at 25°C
41. Place tubes on magnetic stand for 10 seconds
42. Remove supernatant
43. Keep supernatant on ice for subsequent recovery rounds
44. Add 500 microliters of wash buffer A to beads
45. Vortex mixture for five seconds
46. Collect beads using magnet
47. Wash beads twice with 500 microliters of wash buffer B
48. Add 30 microliters of 10-millimolar Tris-HCl to beads
49. Incubate tube at 80 degrees Celsius for two minutes with continuous shaking at 1,000 RPM
50. Transfer tube to magnetic stand and collect eluate within 10 seconds to prevent RNA rebinding
51. Add 30 microliters of streptavidin-coupled magnetic beads to 1 mL binding and wash buffer containing 0.1 mg/mL E. coli tRNA
52. Equilibrate bead mixture on rotator for 1 hour at room temperature
53. Wash beads three times with 750 microliters binding and wash buffer
54. Vortex tube containing washed beads
55. Remove binding and wash buffer from tube
56. Resuspend beads in 30 microliters buffer
57. Store resuspended beads on ice until use
58. Dilute approximately 35 micrograms of total protein from poly(A) isolation in 100 microliters of binding and wash buffer
59. Add 200 picomoles of appropriate antisense oligonucleotide
60. Incubate mixture at 70 degrees Celsius for 5 minutes to facilitate annealing
61. Remove heat block from device and place at room temperature for 10 minutes to cool slowly
62. Add 30 microliters of equilibrated streptavidin-coupled magnetic beads to sample
63. Incubate mixture for 30 minutes at 25 degrees Celsius with constant shaking at 950 rpm
64. Place tube on magnetic stand and remove supernatant
65. Wash beads three times with 750 microliters of pre-warmed binding and wash buffer at 55 degrees Celsius
66. Add 20 microliters of 10-millimolar Tris-HCl
67. Place sample at 90 degrees Celsius with constant shaking at 950 rpm for 10 minutes to elute RNA
68. Place tube in magnetic stand
69. Immediately collect eluate

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Prepare inoculum in 50 microliters of saline
2. Fill 1 mL syringe fitted with sterile bent gavage needle with inoculum
3. Load syringe with 100 microliter air pocket behind inoculum
4. Place anesthetized mouse on angled wooden platform hanging by incisors on wire
5. Gently restrain mouse in place with ribbon
6. Turn on laryngoscope with one hand
7. Grab blunt-tipped forceps with other hand
8. Use laryngoscope tip and forceps to gently pry open mouth
9. Pull tongue out and hold it to the side using forceps
10. Guide laryngoscope blade toward back of mouth
11. Maintain gentle 90-degree downward pressure with laryngoscope until trachea opening is visible
12. Take 1 mL syringe fitted with bent gavage needle containing inoculum
13. Insert needle into trachea until bend reaches front incisors
14. Push plunger evenly to deliver inoculum without bubbling
15. Withdraw needle from trachea immediately after delivery
16. Hold mouse upright for several seconds to facilitate lung inhalation
17. Place mouse near heating lamp for recovery until awake
18. Pin arms and legs of euthanized mouse to dissection board
19. Make midline incision on ventral side with scissors
20. Gently pull skin to expose peritoneum
21. Make incisions on peritoneum to expose abdominal organs
22. Hold tip of sternum with forceps
23. Puncture diaphragm with scissors
24. Cut diaphragm along rib cage sides with scissors parallel to dissection board
25. Cut through thoracic cavity along dorsoventral line
26. Lift ribcage on right side of heart
27. Identify lymph nodes under thymus and near tracheal blood vessel
28. Harvest lymph nodes into 1 ml digestion mix
29. Place lymph node sample on ice
30. Harvest lungs into six-well plate
31. Aspirate PBS from six-well plate kept on ice
32. Chop lung lobes into small pieces using forceps and scissors
33. Hold lymph node down with 26-gauge needle
34. Tease lymph node apart with second 26-gauge needle
35. Add 3 milliliters of digestion mix to lungs
36. Add 1 milliliter of digestion mix to lymph nodes
37. Incubate lymph nodes for 25-30 minutes at 37°C
38. Incubate lungs for 30 minutes at 37°C
39. Add EDTA to final concentration of 10 millimolar to digestion mixtures
40. Place digestion mixtures on ice
41. Pass pieces of lungs through 18-gauge needle using 3ml syringe
42. Mash lung and lymph node pieces through 70-100 micron cell strainers three times
43. Wash cell strainers with 10ml HBSS without calcium and magnesium using back end of 1ml syringe plunger
44. Centrifuge cell samples at 500 × g
45. Resuspend cell pellets in 5 milliliters of red blood cell lysis buffer
46. Incubate suspension for 3 minutes at room temperature
47. Add 10 milliliters of HBSS without calcium and magnesium to quench lysis
48. Centrifuge samples at 500 × g for 5 minutes
49. Bring lung single-cell suspension to 10 milliliters and lymph node suspension to 5 milliliters

6. Incubate plate overnight at 37°C
7. Aspirate gelatin-fibronectin solution from wells

9. Aspirate gelatin fibronectin solution from wells of culture plate

12. Rinse culture briefly with PBS at 37 degrees Celsius
13. Aspirate PBS from flask

15. Gently lower and rotate flask to cover cells with trypsin-EDTA solution
16. Place flask in incubator for 1 minute at 37 degrees Celsius
17. Aspirate trypsin EDTA solution from culture without disturbing cells
18. Add 1.3 milliliters of trypsin EDTA solution to flask
19. Incubate flask at room temperature for one minute
20. Observe cells under microscope to verify detachment from flask surface
21. Gently tap flask to dislodge remaining attached cells
22. Add 1.3 milliliters of soybean trypsin inhibitor solution to cells
23. Transfer cell suspension to 15 milliliter centrifuge tube
24. Rinse empty flask with five milliliters of solution
25. Rinse empty flask with 5 milliliters of wash medium
26. Add rinse medium to cells in 15 milliliter centrifuge tube

28. Aspirate supernatant without disturbing cell pellet
29. Resuspend cell pellet in 6 milliliters of supplemented medium
30. Add 0.5 milliliters of cell suspension to each well of culture plate
31. Incubate plates at 37 degrees Celsius
32. Change medium daily until cultures are confluent
33. Dilute Road Two and RH 237 stock solutions 1:1000 in Hank's salt solution
34. Observe 12-well culture plates under microscope to determine HL-1 cell confluency
35. Gently remove cover slip from well and rinse with Hank's salt solution
36. Place cover slip into 35mm Petri dish containing 3ml Road Two working solution
37. Put Petri dish into 37°C water bath
38. Bubble continuous stream of gas through solution for oxygenation
39. Incubate for 30 minutes to stain cells with calcium-sensitive dye
40. Transfer cover slip to 3 milliliters of oxygenated RH 237 solution
41. Incubate cover slip in RH 237 solution for 15 minutes
42. Place cover slip with double-stained cell monolayer in circulation chamber on inverted fluorescence microscope
43. Adjust chamber flow speed to maintain temperature at 35°C with ≤0.3°C gradient across chamber
44. Flow Hank salt solution across cell monolayer for 5 minutes to remove excess dye
45. Place bipolar electrode in solution near monolayer without touching cells
46. Program electrode to administer pulses of 2 millisecond width for up to 500 milliseconds per cycle
47. Pace monolayer while imaging cells with 40x objective
48. Excite calcium and voltage sensors using LED light source coupled to excitation filter and dichroic mirror
49. Split emitted fluorescence through dichroic mirror to separate calcium and voltage signals
50. Collect fluorescent signals separately with two CCD cameras
51. Image four different areas of monolayer for complete coverage
52. Record signal for less than 2 seconds per imaging field to avoid photobleaching
