prompt:
Question: Given the complete step list of the experiment, please predict the next step that will take place after experimental steps shown in this video.
Complete step list: Warm S2 media in a 28°C water bath for 30 minutes
2. Place transfection reagents, plasmid, and oligonucleotides on ice
3. Aspirate old media from cells using sterile technique in tissue culture hood without disturbing cells
4. Add equivalent volume of fresh warmed media and rinse cells off flask bottom using pipette
5. Adjust cell concentration to 1×10⁶ cells/mL
6. Add 1 mL of adjusted mosquito cells to each well of 6-well plate
7. Transfer plasmid DNA to sterile microcentrifuge tubes
8. Add 99 microliters of EC buffer per microgram of plasmid DNA and LNA ON
9. Add 8 microliters of enhancer per microgram of DNA
10. Vortex DNA-buffer-enhancer mixture for 1 second
11. Briefly centrifuge solution
12. Incubate samples at room temperature for 5 minutes
13. Add 10 microliters of transfection reagent per microgram of plasmid DNA
14. Vortex mixture for 10 seconds
15. Briefly centrifuge solution to bottom of tubes
16. Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes
17. Bring final volume of DNA-buffer-enhancer mixture to 1000 microliters by slowly adding fresh warmed media
18. Gently mix mixture by pipetting up and down 3-4 times
19. Slowly add 1 milliliter of DNA-enhancer mixture to each cell well one drop at a time
20. Gently swirl plate to ensure uniform distribution of cells and transfection mixture
21. Incubate cells under normal growth conditions
22. Gently aspirate media from cells
23. Slowly replace aspirated media with equivalent volume of fresh warmed media
24. Examine positive control cells transfected with GFP-expressing plasmid under fluorescent microscope
25. Aspirate old media from cells requiring thinning
26. Slowly add equivalent volume of fresh warmed media to thinned cells
27. Detach cells from well bottom by pipetting up and down
28. Discard half volume of cell mixture
29. Add 1 mL fresh warmed media to adjust final volume to 2 mL
30. Aspirate old media from cells
31. Add 1 milliliter of sterile room-temperature PBS to each well
32. Detach cells from well bottom by pipetting PBS up and down
33. Transfer cell mixture to 5 milliliter snap cap tubes
34. Immediately analyze cells via flow cytometry
35. Transfect MS Q4 three and gambier UA five B cells with positive control GFP expressing plasmid
36. Transfect SUA five B cells with: GFP expressing plasmid (positive control), BFP expressing plasmid (negative control), and BFP expressing plasmid with increasing concentrations of BFP-specific LNAO ns

1. Weigh 100 milligrams of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA)

4. Place homogenizer in beaker containing 50 milliliters of 1% polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) solution
5. Position homogenizer close to bottom of beaker without touching
6. Turn on homogenizer to appropriate speed
7. Add PLGA solution to beaker for 1 minute of homogenization
8. Pour polyvinyl alcohol PLGA micro-particle solution into beaker containing 100 milliliters of 0.5% PVA solution on stir plate in chemical hood
9. Stir solution for at least four hours
10. Pour particle solution into 50 milliliter conical tubes
11. Collect particles by centrifugation
12. Replace supernatant with 20 milliliters of de-ionized water
13. Re-suspend particles by vortexing
14. Bring final volume in each tube to 50 milliliters with de-ionized water
15. Wash particles two more times using demonstrated procedure
16. Dissolve 200 milligrams of PLGA in 5 milliliters of dichloromethane
17. Place sonicator probe in beaker containing 50 milliliters of 1% PVA solution on ice without touching beaker bottom
18. Begin sonication at 12 watts for 2 minutes
19. Add PLGA solution to beaker during sonication
20. Pour 1% polyvinyl alcohol PLGA nano-particle solution into beaker containing 100 milliliters of 0.5% PVA solution
21. Place beaker on stir plate in chemical fume hood for 4-hour solvent evaporation
22. Pour evaporated particle solution into 50 milliliter conical tubes
23. Centrifuge tubes to remove micro-particles
24. Remove supernatants after centrifugation
25. Transfer nano-particles to high-speed centrifuge tubes for three washes in de-ionized water
26. Re-suspend particles in 1 milliliter of fresh de-ionized water
27. Add film casting solution to achieve 2.5 mg/mL particle concentration
28. Transfer 10 mL aliquots of particle suspension into 75x50 mm rectangular Petri dishes
29. Transfer 15 mL aliquots of particle suspension into 100x100 mm square Petri dishes
30. Remove dried films using tweezers after overnight drying
31. Trim film edges with scissors
32. Place short edges of film between two neoprene rubber pieces
33. Mount film on aluminum blocks of automated thin film stretching device
34. Secure film using Allen wrench to screw metal grips on rubber
35. Mount all four film edges onto aluminum blocks for 2D stretching
36. Measure and record film length between aluminum blocks for 1D or 2D stretching
37. Calculate required stretch distance in one or two directions based on desired fold stretch
38. Place film-loaded stretching device in 90°C oven with water-containing beaker for 10-minute thermal conditioning
39. Let stretched film cool to room temperature for 20 minutes
40. For 1D stretching: Cut film out of stretching device at edges
41. For 2D stretching: Cut out and save center square of uniformly stretched film
42. Place films in 50 mL conical tubes (maximum two films per tube)
43. Add approximately 25 mL de-ionized water to each tube for vortexing
44. When films dissolve: Wash particles three times in de-ionized water as demonstrated
45. After last wash: Re-suspend particles in approximately 1 mL fresh de-ionized water per tube
46. Freeze particles at -80°C for 1 hour or overnight for lyophilization
47. Re-suspend lyophilized micro/nano-particles at 20 mg/mL in freshly prepared MES buffer with vortexing
48. Transfer 100 μL of particle solution to polypropylene micro centrifuge tube containing 900 μL MES buffer
49. Add 100 μL of freshly prepared EDC NHS solution to tube
50. Mix particles by vortexing
51. Incubate particles on inverter at room temperature for 30 minutes
52. Collect particles by centrifugation
53. Re-suspend micro-particle pellets in 1 mL PBS by vortexing
54. Re-suspend nano-particles in 1 mL PBS by 5-second sonication at 2-3 watts
55. Add 8 micrograms of signal one protein and 10 micrograms of anti-mouse CD28 antibody to micro-particles
56. Add 16 micrograms of signal one protein and 20 micrograms of anti-mouse CD28 antibody to nano-particles
57. Bring final volume in each tube to 1.1 milliliter with PBS
58. Incubate particles overnight on inverter at 4 degrees Celsius
59. Wash particles three times in de-ionized water

18. Excise whole transfected leaf

34. Draw water into syringe until approximately half-filled
35. Point syringe upwards

37. Cover tip of syringe

40. Cover surface of microscope slide

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Expel three 50-microliter drops of media at top, middle, and bottom of glass slide using media-filled filter syringe
2. Transfer 5-10 third instar larvae or early pupae to top media drop using dissecting probe
3. Agitate larvae/pupae gently in media with dissecting probe to remove food/debris
4. Turn single larva/pupa on its side using dissecting probe
5. Identify translucent bilateral testes in posterior third of body to confirm male
6. Discard animals lacking testes (females)
7. Transfer clean male larva/pupa to second media drop
8. Repeat transfer until 3-4 male larvae/pupae are in second media drop
9. Grasp animal at mid-region anterior to testes using forceps
10. Tear animal in half gently using second pair of forceps
11. Secure posterior end of animal on glass slide using forceps
12. Push down on cuticle adjacent to forceps using scalpel edge
13. Move scalpel toward cut end of animal to expel internal organs
14. Gently tease apart testes from surrounding organs
15. Transfer testes individually by inserting scalpel edge under fat body, lifting tissue from media, and moving to third drop
16. Use prewetted glass Pasteur pipette for transfer if insufficient fat body remains attached for scalpel lifting
17. Trim excess fat body from testes using sharp end of scalpel in third media drop, leaving small rim around edges
18. Deposit 30 microliters of Schneider's medium at center of 50mm gas-permeable culture dish using filter syringe
19. Transfer up to five prepared testes to medium drop using scalpel tool or prewetted Pasteur pipette
20. Position testes centrally on gas-permeable membrane using scalpel tool
21. Place four drops of halocarbon oil around medium drop using 1ml syringe, positioned at coverslip corners
22. Align 22mm glass coverslip corners with oil drops and lower coverslip onto media/oil
23. Place culture dish under dissecting microscope
24. Insert corner of delicate task wipe under coverslip
25. Wick away media until coverslip contacts surface of largest testis
26. Place drop of immersion oil on glass coverslip above testes
27. Turn over dish
28. Place dish on microscope stage
29. Move 40X or 60X microscope objective into oil below testes
30. Use transmitted light to locate single testis
31. Bring testis into focus
32. Place 0.5 milliliters of 8% paraformaldehyde in PBSTx into one well of a nine-well dissecting dish
33. Transfer up to 10 testes to the well using a glass Pasteur pipette
34. Ensure testes are positioned at the bottom of the well
35. Transfer testes to a new well containing 0.5 milliliters of PBSTx after 20 minutes
36. Wash testes by agitating gently for five minutes
37. Wash testes two additional times in new wells with fresh PBSTx
38. Transfer testes from dissecting dish to a 1.5 milliliter microcentrifuge tube containing diluted primary antibody
39. Incubate tube overnight at 4°C with gentle rocking or nutation
40. Transfer testes from nine well plate to glass microscopy slide using Pasteur pipette
41. Use scalpel edge to push testes down onto slide surface if necessary
42. Wick away excess liquid from testes using corner of delicate task wipe
43. Remove as much liquid as possible from testes
44. Apply 30-50 microliter drop of microscopy mounting medium to testes
45. Place 22 millimeter coverslip onto drop of mounting medium
46. Allow coverslip to settle and mounting medium to spread under coverslip
47. Apply gentle pressure to coverslip if necessary to squeeze out excess mounting medium and allow coverslip to rest on testes

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Open thoracic cavity
2. Clear blood from vasculature through intraoral perfusion of PBS with heparin
3. Inject casting agent into left ventricle to perfuse circulation system
4. Remove perfused brain and fix in Paraformaldehyde
5. Dehydrate and clarify brain tissue with ethanol and methyl salicylate
6. Anesthetize mouse via intraperitoneal injection of ketamine and xylazine diluted in saline
7. Confirm full anesthesia by paw pinch test
8. Make chest incision below xiphoid process using scissors
9. Cut through diaphragm
10. Cut between dorsal and ventral segments of ribcage
11. Fold up sternum and adjacent chest wall
12. Secure folded tissue with hemostat to expose pericardial sac
13. Open pericardial sac using tweezers if necessary
14. Open pericardial sac with tweezers to expose heart
15. Begin perfusing PBS with 5 units/mL heparin at 37°C using pump set to 100 mmHg
16. Insert blunt 22-gauge needle connected to pump outflow into left ventricle near heart apex
17. Cut open right atrium to enable blood outflow and continue perfusion until blood is removed from circulation
18. Mix 5 mL of diluent with 4 mL of filtered compound
19. Add 450 μL of curing agent to mixture
20. Mix casting agent solution immediately before use
21. Draw casting agent solution into 10 mL syringe
22. Attach blunt 20-gauge needle to syringe
23. Fill attached needle with solution
24. Insert needle into left ventricle through existing hole
25. Secure needle in place with hemostat clamp
26. Manually inject casting agent solution into left ventricle at 3 ml/min
27. Monitor for perfusion indicators: casting agent in intestine/liver vasculature, distal limb discoloration, nose/tongue discoloration
28. Readjust needle position if necessary to achieve proper perfusion
29. Remove brain
30. Place brain in 4% paraformaldehyde overnight at 4°C
31. Dehydrate brain in 25% ethanol at room temperature (initiating 7-day ethanol series)
32. Immerse perfused brain in methyl salicylate for 2 days at room temperature to clarify tissue around blood vessels

1. Weigh 100 milligrams of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA)

20. Pour 1% polyvinyl alcohol PLGA nano-particle solution into beaker containing 100 milliliters of 0.5% PVA solution
21. Place beaker on stir plate in chemical fume hood for 4-hour solvent evaporation
22. Pour evaporated particle solution into 50 milliliter conical tubes
23. Centrifuge tubes to remove micro-particles
24. Remove supernatants after centrifugation
25. Transfer nano-particles to high-speed centrifuge tubes for three washes in de-ionized water
26. Re-suspend particles in 1 milliliter of fresh de-ionized water
27. Add film casting solution to achieve 2.5 mg/mL particle concentration
28. Transfer 10 mL aliquots of particle suspension into 75x50 mm rectangular Petri dishes
29. Transfer 15 mL aliquots of particle suspension into 100x100 mm square Petri dishes
30. Remove dried films using tweezers after overnight drying
31. Trim film edges with scissors
32. Place short edges of film between two neoprene rubber pieces
33. Mount film on aluminum blocks of automated thin film stretching device
34. Secure film using Allen wrench to screw metal grips on rubber
35. Mount all four film edges onto aluminum blocks for 2D stretching
36. Measure and record film length between aluminum blocks for 1D or 2D stretching
37. Calculate required stretch distance in one or two directions based on desired fold stretch
38. Place film-loaded stretching device in 90°C oven with water-containing beaker for 10-minute thermal conditioning
39. Let stretched film cool to room temperature for 20 minutes
40. For 1D stretching: Cut film out of stretching device at edges
41. For 2D stretching: Cut out and save center square of uniformly stretched film
42. Place films in 50 mL conical tubes (maximum two films per tube)
43. Add approximately 25 mL de-ionized water to each tube for vortexing
44. When films dissolve: Wash particles three times in de-ionized water as demonstrated
45. After last wash: Re-suspend particles in approximately 1 mL fresh de-ionized water per tube
46. Freeze particles at -80°C for 1 hour or overnight for lyophilization
47. Re-suspend lyophilized micro/nano-particles at 20 mg/mL in freshly prepared MES buffer with vortexing
48. Transfer 100 μL of particle solution to polypropylene micro centrifuge tube containing 900 μL MES buffer
49. Add 100 μL of freshly prepared EDC NHS solution to tube
50. Mix particles by vortexing
51. Incubate particles on inverter at room temperature for 30 minutes
52. Collect particles by centrifugation
53. Re-suspend micro-particle pellets in 1 mL PBS by vortexing
54. Re-suspend nano-particles in 1 mL PBS by 5-second sonication at 2-3 watts
55. Add 8 micrograms of signal one protein and 10 micrograms of anti-mouse CD28 antibody to micro-particles
56. Add 16 micrograms of signal one protein and 20 micrograms of anti-mouse CD28 antibody to nano-particles
57. Bring final volume in each tube to 1.1 milliliter with PBS
58. Incubate particles overnight on inverter at 4 degrees Celsius
59. Wash particles three times in de-ionized water

3. Agitate larvae/pupae gently in media with dissecting probe to remove food/debris
4. Turn single larva/pupa on its side using dissecting probe
5. Identify translucent bilateral testes in posterior third of body to confirm male
6. Discard animals lacking testes (females)

9. Grasp animal at mid-region anterior to testes using forceps

11. Secure posterior end of animal on glass slide using forceps
12. Push down on cuticle adjacent to forceps using scalpel edge
13. Move scalpel toward cut end of animal to expel internal organs
14. Gently tease apart testes from surrounding organs
15. Transfer testes individually by inserting scalpel edge under fat body, lifting tissue from media, and moving to third drop
16. Use prewetted glass Pasteur pipette for transfer if insufficient fat body remains attached for scalpel lifting
17. Trim excess fat body from testes using sharp end of scalpel in third media drop, leaving small rim around edges
18. Deposit 30 microliters of Schneider's medium at center of 50mm gas-permeable culture dish using filter syringe
19. Transfer up to five prepared testes to medium drop using scalpel tool or prewetted Pasteur pipette
20. Position testes centrally on gas-permeable membrane using scalpel tool

22. Align 22mm glass coverslip corners with oil drops and lower coverslip onto media/oil
23. Place culture dish under dissecting microscope
24. Insert corner of delicate task wipe under coverslip
25. Wick away media until coverslip contacts surface of largest testis
26. Place drop of immersion oil on glass coverslip above testes
27. Turn over dish
28. Place dish on microscope stage
29. Move 40X or 60X microscope objective into oil below testes
30. Use transmitted light to locate single testis
31. Bring testis into focus
32. Place 0.5 milliliters of 8% paraformaldehyde in PBSTx into one well of a nine-well dissecting dish
33. Transfer up to 10 testes to the well using a glass Pasteur pipette
34. Ensure testes are positioned at the bottom of the well
35. Transfer testes to a new well containing 0.5 milliliters of PBSTx after 20 minutes
36. Wash testes by agitating gently for five minutes
37. Wash testes two additional times in new wells with fresh PBSTx
38. Transfer testes from dissecting dish to a 1.5 milliliter microcentrifuge tube containing diluted primary antibody
39. Incubate tube overnight at 4°C with gentle rocking or nutation
40. Transfer testes from nine well plate to glass microscopy slide using Pasteur pipette
41. Use scalpel edge to push testes down onto slide surface if necessary
42. Wick away excess liquid from testes using corner of delicate task wipe
43. Remove as much liquid as possible from testes
44. Apply 30-50 microliter drop of microscopy mounting medium to testes
45. Place 22 millimeter coverslip onto drop of mounting medium
46. Allow coverslip to settle and mounting medium to spread under coverslip
47. Apply gentle pressure to coverslip if necessary to squeeze out excess mounting medium and allow coverslip to rest on testes

18. Press PDMS surface onto cleaned coverslip for bonding
19. Confirm bond integrity by testing for detachment when pulling coverslip slightly
20. Secure 90-degree blunt needle with pliers
21. Insert one end of needle into Tygon tube
22. Insert other end of needle into punched hole of device
23. Repeat needle-tubing assembly process for remaining device holes

29. Secure tubing to outer walls of aluminum box housing adhesive tape
30. Inject 4-5 microliters of antifreeze protein solution into inlet channel using glass syringe

32. Initiate temperature control program

39. Slowly inject buffer solution into second inlet of microfluidic device
40. Observe decrease in fluorescent signal using NIS-Elements Imaging Program

42. Slowly increase temperature until all ice melts while preserving hydrates
43. Hold temperature at 1°C for 3 minutes
44. Set temperature to -2°C
45. Observe hydrate abundance in microfluidic channels under inhibitor-free conditions
46. Inject antifreeze protein or inhibitor into microfluidic channel using glass syringe
47. Adjust temperature to maintain crystal stability
48. Allow inhibitor molecules to adsorb to crystal surface for several minutes

50. Capture images of crystal before and after solution exchange

1. Lay surgical drape
2. Arrange instruments for gross dissection

4. Set up bio safety cabinet for dish assembly
5. Set up open globe injury induction workspace inside bio safety cabinet
6. Position cross tracking vice on lab jack in front of puncture platform
7. Wash eyes with antibiotic antimycotic PBS
8. Place eye on antibiotic antimycotic PBS-soaked gauze
9. Create incision near eye equator using sterile razorblade or scalpel

14. Extend cut 360 degrees around iris to expose entire trabecular meshwork region
15. Clean residual iris covering trabecular meshwork if necessary
16. Trim ciliary body remnants posterior to trabecular meshwork region
17. Leave one millimeter thin band of tissue
18. Wet cotton swab in media and gently dab center of cornea to remove pigment
19. Hold eyes with forceps and wipe extra pigment around sclera
20. Place inverted anterior segment over elevated region of bottom dish with cornea centered
21. Position clamping ring on top of anterior segment
22. Tighten screws gently with L-key

24. Attach 18 gauge 90-degree bent needle hub to first fluidic connector
25. Attach length of tubing to first fluidic connector
26. Attach 18 gauge needle hub to first fluidic connector
27. Attach nylon syringe filter to first fluidic connector
28. Attach three-way valve to first fluidic connector
29. Attach 20 millimeter media-filled syringe to first fluidic connector
30. Attach 18-gauge 90-degree bent needle hub, tubing, 18-gauge needle hub, three-way valve, and 10ml syringe barrel to second fluidic connector
31. Keep three-way valves open to syringes
32. Gently push media through system via first fluidics connector port
33. Remove bubbles by gently pushing media into dish
34. Invert dish to push out bubbles
35. Place anterior segment organ culture dish into cell culture incubator
36. Direct tubing lines out through bottom of incubator door
37. Position tubing lines with reservoir at pressure transducer instrument
38. Connect side three-way valve to pressure transducer setup while PBS flows through line
39. Set pressure regulator on puncture platform to 50 PSI
40. Position cross-tracking vice on lab jack in front of puncture platform
41. Extend piston arm to maximal distance
42. Position corneal apex within 1 mm region of puncturing object
43. Retract piston arm
44. Bring anterior segment 1 cm closer to puncturing object
45. Turn on puncture device
46. Open solenoid valve with second switch
47. Press second switch to retract device from eye
48. Verify injury induction via visual inspection and media leakage from injury site
49. Assess corneal epithelium integrity using optical coherence tomography
50. Image injured anterior segment tissue immediately after injury
51. Image injured anterior segment tissue 72 hours post-injury

22. Set cutting device to cut two millimeter lengths of tubing
23. Cut tubing using cutting device
24. Incubate cut modules in 50 milliliter conical tube at 37 degrees Celsius for 60 minutes
25. Vortex to remove collagen modules from tubing
26. Vortex 50 liter conical tube containing modules at medium speed for 10 seconds
27. Allow modules to settle to bottom of tube for 5 minutes
28. Transfer settled modules to 15 milliliter conical tube using wide mouth 10 milliliter serological pipette
29. Vortex 15 milliliter conical tube
30. Allow modules to settle after first vortex
31. Transfer settled modules from second vortex to 15 milliliter tube
32. Transfer settled modules from third vortex to 15 milliliter tube
33. Adjust media volume in tube to five milliliters
34. Remove media from cells
35. Wash cells with PBS
36. Add 3 ml of trypsin EDTA
37. Incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes
38. Resuspend cells in 7 ml of media
39. Transfer cell suspension to 15 ml tube
40. Count cells using hemocytometer
41. Pellet cells at 300 G for 5 minutes
42. Resuspend cell pellet in 5 ml endothelial cell media
43. Add 5 ml media containing endothelial cells to modules
44. Incubate modules with endothelial cells statically and dynamically
45. Mix modules with endothelial cells by inversion
46. Set tube upright at 37°C for 15 minutes
47. Invert tube again
48. Incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes
49. Rock 15 mL tube gently at 37°C for 60 minutes (dynamic incubation)
50. Transfer modules to non-tissue culture treated plate
51. Incubate overnight at 37°C
52. Transfer modules to new non-tissue culture treated plate with fresh media

25. Melt agarose mixture in research-grade microwave for up to two minutes

33. Incubate cells for five minutes at 37 degrees Celsius
34. Add two milliliters of soybean trypsin inhibitor to plate
35. Wash cells from plate into 15 milliliter tube
36. Centrifuge at 250 times G for five minutes
37. Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL PBS
38. Quantify cells using Trypan Blue staining
39. Aliquot 20,000 normal human keratinocytes in 100 μL KSFM-SCM
40. Seed cells in each well of prepared 96-well plate
41. Incubate plate overnight
42. Analyze seeded wells for epidermis sphere formation using inverted phase contrast microscope
43. Add 4 ml of prewarmed KSFM-SCM at 37°C to six-centimeter dish
44. Transfer single spheroid to plate using wide-bore 1 ml pipette tip
45. Incubate plate overnight
46. Analyze seeded spheroid for attaching/propagating cells using inverted phase contrast microscope
47. Remove media from plate
48. Add 2 ml of fresh KSFM-SCM media to plate
49. Quantify cell viability using Trypan Blue and automated cell counter
50. Aliquot 100 microliters containing 100,000 to 4 million keratinocytes into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes
51. Place tubes on ice in dark environment by turning off laminar hood lights
52. Add 2 μL FITC-conjugated anti-integrin alpha six and 2 μL PE-conjugated anti-EGFR to tubes for 1:50 dilution
53. Prepare tube without antibodies for unstained control
54. Incubate tubes on ice in dark for 30 minutes
55. Perform flow cytometry analysis with appropriate lasers
56. Use negative and positive controls to establish gates
57. Sort epidermal stem cell fraction, proliferative progenitor fraction, and committed progenitor fraction
58. Transfer sorted cells from sorting tubes into 15 ml conical tubes containing 10x volume of PBS
59. Centrifuge tubes at 250 × g for 5 minutes
60. Remove supernatant from tubes
61. Resuspend pellet in 4 mL of KSFM-SCM
62. Transfer resuspended cells to 6 cm plate
63. Incubate plate overnight at 37°C in 5% CO₂ incubator with 95% humidity
64. Remove media from plates
65. Add 4 mL of prewarmed KSFM-SCM (37°C) to plates
66. Repeat media change with 4 mL prewarmed KSFM-SCM every 3 days until 70-80% confluency

31. Quantitate diluted cell suspensions using hemocytometer under microscope

33. Swab insect injection surface with 95% ethanol
34. Inject 10 microliters of cell suspension into insect at <45° angle behind abdominal proleg
35. Plate 10⁻² to 10⁻⁶ dilutions on middle of agar plate
36. Let samples flow toward bottom of plate
37. Incubate plates at appropriate temperature
38. Count colonies to enumerate inoculum
39. Inject three to five insects with sterile PBS for negative control group
40. Incubate all insects at 26°C with 16-hour light/8-hour dark photoperiod
41. Monitor insect survival over time after injections
42. Inject insects with approximately 50 CFU of wild type or attenuated mutant strain of Xer Haus NLA grown to mid-log phase

prompt:
Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Place one cotton ball in bottom of 4cm diameter × 21cm height conical plastic pot
2. Fill pot with steam-pasteurized soil mixture to 2cm below rim
3. Insert plastic stake designating genotype into pot
4. Plant one seed of corresponding cotton genotype in pot
5. Cover seed with additional soil
6. Transfer pots to growth chamber set at 28°C with 16-hour fluorescent/incandescent photoperiod
7. Place water emitters into each pot
8. Use automatic watering system to water pots twice daily
9. Create small depression in soil next to each plant
10. Add 1 mL reniform nematode suspension into each depression
11. Use scissors to remove most fully expanded leaves from plants
12. Squeeze pot and slide soil into hand to remove plants
13. Agitate root system in 10L tap water container to remove soil
14. Rinse root system briefly in container of clean tap water
15. Use scissors to remove cleaned root system 1cm below soil line
16. Place roots into 120ml plastic container
17. Place root system below soil line into 120 ml plastic specimen container
18. Cover root system with approximately 30 ml red food coloring solution
19. Microwave specimen container until staining solution begins to boil
20. Replace food coloring solution with 100 ml tap water after cooling to room temperature
21. Place cover on specimen container and refrigerate at 4°C
22. Place cotton ball in bottom of new conical plastic pot and partially fill with peat moss potting medium
23. Place one harvested vegetative shoot with root system in pot
24. Firmly add potting medium to fill pot
25. Place labeled plastic stake in pot to designate cotton genotype
26. Place tray of pots into plastic container of water
27. Water plants briefly to moisten potting medium
28. Place pots in growth chamber set to 28°C with 16-hour photoperiod
29. Partially fill six-liter plastic pot with potting medium (after ~30 days)
30. Transfer plant into six-liter pot while firmly adding potting medium
31. Remove root sample from specimen container
32. Use stereo microscope at 20X magnification to count female nematodes attached to root system
33. Place root system on paper towels for 10 minutes to remove excess moisture
34. Weigh root system to determine fresh root weight

Question: Given the complete step list of the experiment, please predict the next step that will take place after experimental steps shown in this video.
Complete step list: Add 2 microliters of 1 mg/mL antibody to 200 microliters of cell lysates
2. Incubate lysate-antibody mixture at 4°C for 1 hour while rocking
3. Wash protein A-Sepharose beads 2-3 times by adding lysis buffer
4. Centrifuge beads at 4°C for 30 seconds to 1 minute at 5000 × g
5. Remove supernatant from beads using pipet
6. Resuspend beads in buffer
7. Add 30 microliters of 50% protein A-Sepharose bead slurry in lysis buffer to lysates
8. Incubate lysate-bead mixture at 4°C for 1 hour while rocking
9. Perform touch spin at 4°C to pellet beads
10. Remove supernatant after bead pelleting
11. Wash beads three times with 1 mL bead wash buffer including touch spinning
12. Wash beads once with 1X kinase reaction buffer
13. Perform touch spin prior to buffer removal
14. Remove maximum buffer without disturbing beads
15. Add entire reaction mixture to kinase sample
16. Incubate reaction at 30 degrees Celsius
17. Place reaction on ice
18. Add 7.5 microliters of 5X Laemmli sample buffer
19. Heat reaction at 100 degrees Celsius for 3-5 minutes in heat block
20. Load 20 microliters of sample per well onto 10-15% SDS-PAGE gel
21. Shield gel apparatus to limit phosphorus-32 radiation exposure
22. Run SDS-PAGE gel to separate kinase and substrate by molecular weight
23. Remove gel from glass and aluminum plates
24. Place gel in 50 milliliters of Coomassie stain
25. Shake gel on orbital shaker at 50 RPM for one hour
26. Transfer gel from stain to fixing solution
27. Place foam pieces or knotted laboratory wipes in container with gel
28. Rock gel in 600-700 milliliters of fixing solution on orbital shaker at 50 RPM overnight
29. Remove gel from fixing solution
30. Soak gel in 200 milliliters of methanol with gentle agitation
31. Continue agitation for 1-2 minutes until gel turns milky white
32. Wet a 14 cm × 14 cm piece of qualitative filter paper with methanol
33. Place methanol-treated filter paper onto slab gel vacuum dryer
34. Lay gel onto filter paper with front side facing up
35. Cover gel carefully with plastic wrap
36. Turn on and run vacuum dryer to apply vacuum
37. Roll out air bubbles with soft rubber brayer after vacuum attainment
38. Continue vacuum drying run for 90 minutes
39. Remove dried gel
40. Attach autorad marker (e.g., phosphorescent ruler or dot) to filter paper on gel side
41. Place gel in cassette containing intensifying screen
42. Use Geiger counter to check radioactive signal intensity
43. Place X-ray film on top of dried gel inside film cassette with intensifying screen
44. Remove film from cassette after exposure
45. Develop film in medical/X-ray film processor
46. Mark bands corresponding to protein standards on film
47. Label protein standards and reaction lanes for reference
48. Excise bands from gel corresponding to bands of interest on film
49. Place excised bands in seven milliliter scintillation vials
50. Add four milliliters of scintillation fluid to vials
51. Count bands using liquid scintillation counter
52. Confirm scintillation counter is set to phosphorus-32 energy spectrum window

Question: Based on the full experimental procedure，determine the step numbers shown in the video.
1. Prepare yeast extract with supplements without adenine (YES), Pombe Glutamate Medium (PMG), and PMG without adenine
2. Mix media components according to specified table
3. Add G418 to media after autoclaving if necessary
4. Stir media for 5-10 minutes
5. Aliquot media into 90 milliliter Petri dishes
6. Store plates at 4 degrees Celsius
7. Use cloned rpt4 positive with 5' and 3' UTRs and silent mutation
8. Perform error-prone PCR with primers p5 and p6 and error-prone polymerase in 50 microliter total volume
9. Inoculate 10 milliliters of YES medium with yeast
10. Incubate culture for >16 hours to saturation
11. Dilute cells to OD600 0.2 using 200 milliliters of YES medium
12. Incubate culture at 30°C with shaking for 5-6 hours to OD600 0.6-0.8
13. Calculate volume of cells equivalent to OD600 of 30
14. Dispense cells into four 50ml conical tubes
15. Chill tubes on ice for 10 minutes
16. Harvest cells by centrifugation at 1050 G, 4°C for 3 minutes
17. Place microfuge tubes with cassette DNA and 10 electro cuvettes on ice
18. Discard supernatant while keeping tubes on ice
19. Add 15ml of 1.2M sorbitol
20. Gently shake tubes to resuspend cells
21. Centrifuge at 1050 G, 4°C for 3 minutes
22. Discard supernatant and perform second sorbitol wash
23. Discard supernatant after second centrifugation
24. Resuspend cells and transfer to one 15ml conical tube
25. Add 1.2 molar sorbitol up to 2.4 milliliters
26. Keep tube of cells on ice
27. Add 200 microliters of sorbitol-suspended cells to tube containing fusion PCR construct
28. Mix sample well
29. Transfer sample to electro cuvette
30. Add 600 microliters of 1.2-molar sorbitol to each electroporation cuvette
31. Spread transformed cells onto four YES plates
32. Incubate plates at 30 degrees Celsius for 24 hours
33. Perform replica plating on YES plates containing G418
34. Incubate replica plates for three additional days
35. Perform replica plating from YES plus G418 plates to YES without adenine plates
36. Perform replica plating from YES plus G418 plates to PMG without adenine plates
37. Incubate replica plates at 30°C for 1-2 days until colonies on YES without adenine plates show white coloration
38. Compare growth on YES without adenine and PMG without adenine plates
39. Select colonies showing pink or white coloration on YES without adenine plates with concurrent growth on PMG without adenine plates
40. Exclude colonies without growth on PMG without adenine plates (false positives)
41. Pick each colony and add to 10 microliters of SPZ solution containing 2.5 mg/ml zymolyase 100T
42. Incubate colonies at 37°C for at least 30 minutes
43. Use 1 microliter of incubated solution as template for colony PCR
44. Mark colonies with XhoI-cut PCR products and patch them to YES plus G418 plates
45. Isolate genomic DNA (gDNA) from fission yeast cells
46. Sequence PCR products
47. Compare obtained sequence with wild-type sequence
48. Identify mutations through sequence comparison
49. Re-introduce identified mutations into wild-type cells
50. Confirm phenotype using spotting assay in newly-made mutant cells

38. Drain aqueous E. coli layer into waste beaker

1. Direct neodymium YAG laser output to 1064nm-pass beam splitter

10. Connect digital delay generator output to synchronize neodymium YAG flash lamps at 10 Hz
11. Route another digital delay output through sink box to trigger diode array intensifier and optical multichannel analyzer at 50 Hz
12. Relay adjustable laser trigger output to oscilloscope and pulse generator
13. Connect pulse generator outputs to intensified linear diode array and oscilloscope
14. Connect intensified linear DDE to optical multi-channel analyzer
15. Take necessary safety precautions for working with lasers
16. Set function generator to output 50 hertz triangular pulse
17. Prepare laser by initiating cooling system and power supply
18. Activate laser on digital pulse generator
19. Set gate width for DIO array exposure to plasma radiation
20. Set delay time for data collection after breakdown
21. Initiate optical breakdown in air, image microplasma onto spectrometer slit, and record data
22. Place standard calibration lamps at plasma formation site
23. Fit collected emission data to known wavelengths
24. Turn on tungsten lamp

26. Turn on tungsten lamp

28. Measure lamp temperature using optical porometer
29. Position lamp at plasma creation location
30. Record lamp spectrum using apparatus
31. Compute black body curve using measured temperature
32. Compare computed black body curve to measured spectrum per spectrometer region
33. Determine ideal-to-recorded intensity ratio as function of wavelength
